chapters.title: Chapter 1823 Leave it to me.
paragraphs: "How did you do it?"
"Do what?"

"How did you extend their lifespan? They are only Pseudo Transcendent yet have lived for hundreds of thousands of years. Doesn't that go against the Universe's Rules? The Universe should already be roaring to devour them. Why isn't it reacting?
How are you breaking the Universe's Rules without it retaliating in any way?"
Nux couldn't understand.
In his case, every time he tries to break the Universe's Rules, it cries like a bitch and causes fuss all over the place. Then how come it isn't reacting when the Progenitors do the same thing?
How are the Progenitors outliving other beings? Nux hadn't seen something like this even in a High-Level World like Umbrasol.
Hearing that question, Aeliana, Vyriana, and even the Progenitors turned towards Azriel. seemed that even they didn't know the answer to this question.
"Aren't you breaking the Universe's Rules yourself? Why do you ask?"
"Every time I break the rules, I face consequences. I face its retaliation. That doesn't seem to be the case for you."
Nux's answer was quick.
"This is why an overabundance of knowledge is detrimental."
Azriel suddenly sighed.
"What does that mean?"
Nux questioned with a frown, and Azriel, who observed his expression for a while, questioned with a light chuckle,
"Do you even know how many Universe's 'Rules' have been broken around you till now?"
Hearing that question, Nux's frown deepened as he started thinking.
Not wanting to waste more time, Azriel just continued,
"Transcendent Level Beings who don't have Laws, do you think the Universe would normally allow that? Do you think it would let beings it doesn't acknowledge reach the Transcendent Level?
A level where one is supposed to transcend the understanding of their Law and reach absolute Perfection. How can a being reach this level when they don't even have a Law to begin with?
Do you think it aligns with the Universe's Rules?"
Nux didn't have any answer.

"Azriel Origin died, yet Yrniel was somehow able to keep a Progenitor's Blood and even hand it over to another being, essentially creating another Progenitor. Do you think that aligns with the Universe's Rules?"
"But there was only one Progenitor, just like the Universe intends to. You didn't break any rule-"

"Sure, we didn't break that rule, but according to the so-called 'Rules,' Azriel's Origin's entire existence should have returned to the Universe. That includes his Blood. How was Yrniel able to keep the Blood safe?"
Again, Nux was silent. However, the Vampire Progenitor wasn't done yet.

"Even your father, that Chaos Progenitor. He exists despite being dead. Sure, he uses Ethereal Form to lower his presence, but in the end, even he is breaking the Universe's Rules by not returning to it, no?
Then comes your most recent encounter with an anomaly,
The Reaper's Veil.
A Veil that could hide everything even from the Universe. Do you think that makes any sense? Do you think its existence can be explained using the Universe's Rules?"
"What are you trying to say, Father?"
Aeliana questioned with a solemn look on her face. At her question, the rest present stared at Azriel as well.
"I am saying that the Universe's 'Rules' are full of loopholes. If you study the rules deeply enough and experiment,
You can find more of these loopholes and use them to your advantage."
"But the biggest problem we faced was the lack of information, no? We didn't even know about the Universe's existence, let alone its rules and the possible loopholes in them.
How did we manage to use these loopholes?"
Faustina questioned.
"We didn't use them."
Azriel shook his head.
"Yrniel did."
"What...?"
"Yrniel is the reincarnation of a Supreme World."
"It retained some of its memories, like it retained some memories of my System."
Nux realized, and Azriel nodded.
"That is correct.
Supreme Worlds, Worlds that exist for trillions of years. If anyone would know more about these loopholes..."
"It would be these Supreme Worlds."
Nux completed Azriel's sentence, and the Vampire nodded again.
"This is why I told you to go out and explore more.
Our enemies aren't weak, even if we surpass them in might.
What they know far surpasses what we do.
You cannot possibly surpass them in the information area, but at the very least, you need to reach a level where you wouldn't be caught completely off guard by their
tricks."
Azriel spoke, and Nux nodded with a determined look on his face.
"You have been seeing instances where the Universe's Rules are being broken constantly, and you will continue to see them.
Study them and learn.
The more loopholes you find out about, the better it would be for you."
Azriel instructed, and Nux nodded again.
"Go and take part in the War like you intended to."
Azriel commanded as he then turned towards his daughter and, after a slight pause,
"Take Lia with you."
His words surprised not just Nux and the Progenitors but even Aeliana herself.
"Father, I still wish to spend some time with yo-"
"I will be returning to Yrniel's Core and sleep,"
Azriel revealed.
"What!? No! I cannot allo-"
"Hundreds of years have passed, Aeliana.
All this time, I have been trying to find a way out, a way to coexist with Yrniel without having to destroy mortal life, but Yrniel's energy is intertwined with too many things

If I continue to stay awake, the life in Yrniel will perish. The new-borns will be mortals, unable to cultivate. The cultivators would never be able to advance to the next stage. In all these years, many have lost their lives. This cannot continue.
I am sure even you do not want that."
"But I..."
"Don't worry. I already found a solution."
Azriel spoke as he gently placed his hand on Aeliana's cheek.
"A solution...?"
Acliana glanced at her father with a hopeful look on her face.
Azriel then stared at Nux and,
"I will be leaving things to you.
Don't make me wait for long."
Yes, the so-called 'Solution' was Nux.
'Fuck, I knew something was gonna happen when the stingy old man gave his
daughter away so quickly.
It couldn't have been a more obvious flag, and I can't believe I still fell for it.'
Nux cursed in his head, but in the end, he glanced at his father-in-law and nodded.
"Leave it to me."

chapters.title: Chapter 1824 Yrniel had healed.
paragraphs: Rumble Rumble Rumble
Crack
A crack of radiant light tore through the gray, turbulent skies, splitting clouds into perfect halves.
The ground rumbled in response.
Mana materialized into clean, straight streams that spread across the sky, forming an organized, checkered pattern.
Thunder Thunder Thunder
Whoosh Whoosh Whoosh
The clouds roared, the winds flew-it was as if the very world was expressing its emotions.
However, this emotion wasn't anger.
It was joy.
And this joy was accompanied by some sadness.
Of course, no one could understand its complex emotions.

In a small village nestled near the hills of Yrniel, a farmer paused mid-swing of his scythe as the blades of grass beneath him began to shimmer, their green color deepening as if some form of magical energy was being infused into them.

He blinked, rubbing his eyes. Hearing the clouds' roars, he looked up, and his eyes widened in surprise as he stared at the wide, radiant crack and that organized pattern that had formed all over the sky.
"What in the world...?"
He muttered.
In the heart of the capital, people stopped in their tracks, surprised by the fantasy-like sight.
"What the hell is happening...?"
"Wait... those lines... are they made from Mana...?"
One of the cultivators questioned as he pointed at the sky.
"Have you lost your mind? How long has it been since you were able to manipulate your Mana and form such a clean pattern?"
Another cultivator dismissed with a wave of his hand. He sounded bitter and grumpy. There were wrinkles all over his face, and it was clear the man didn't have much time
left.
"I... I can control mana again..."
Suddenly, a voice was heard.
In an instant, everyone turned toward the voice.
"I... I feel mana flowing properly again!"
Another shout was heard.
The old cultivator closed his trembling eyes.

The mana, once unresponsive, jagged, and chaotic, now swirled around him like a gentle stream, eager to be shaped as he willed. Without waiting, he started absorbing the mana, and the process couldn't have been smoother.
The moment the mana settled into his body, the cultivator opened his eyes. His previous annoyance was now replaced with unhidden joy and excitement.
"I can cultivate again!"
He shouted, tears streaming down his face.
It wasn't just him-all the cultivators were the same, their emotions bursting out of control.
Inside a room, a child tugged at her mother's sleeve, her eyes wide.
"Mama, does this mean I can be a cultivator now?"
The woman's voice broke as she pulled the child into a hug.
"Yes, my love. Yes, it does."
Her tears streamed down her cheeks without stop.
Every day, she prayed.

She prayed and prayed that mana would return to normal because she knew that if it didn't, in the next hundred years, her daughter would die. She would outlive her daughter, and just the thought of that ripped her heart into pieces.
She was afraid-so very afraid-but now...
A smile filled with relief appeared on her face. Her daughter wouldn't die. She wouldn't have to see another one of her children grow old and lose their life.
"Come here.
Let me teach you our family's cultivation technique."
The woman spoke with a smile filled with endless love.
"Yay!"
The little girl was overjoyed.
"It's back,"
Alaric, the King of Vampires, who was observing his people from his castle, whispered.
Feeling the mana that had now returned to normal placed a smile on his face. His eyes fell on the vampires who had already started cultivating, and without having
to look, he knew the rest of the cultivators in Yrniel were doing the same.
Yrniel had healed.
It was the day that marked the end of the Mana Apocalypse.
It was the day where every conflict came to a momentary halt as every cultivator either cultivated or taught the cultivation process to their loved ones.
Some, left without a family and with limited time, even decided to teach their family's cultivation techniques to mortals.
It was a day that would bring forth an entirely new generation of cultivators.
"He is gone..."
However, not everyone was happy.
Aeliana, who was observing the changes in Yrniel and the dimensions connected to it,
realized that her father had returned to his slumber again.
Once again, she would have to live a life without her father next to her.
"Don't worry, we will wake him up soon enough, I promise."
Suddenly, the woman heard some reassuring words as she felt someone holding her
hand.
Knowing who it was, she tightened her grip on his hand and closed her eyes. Her heavy heart eased a little.
After all, she knew these weren't empty words. This man had set everything right and changed her life before. Aeliana knew he would do it again, no matter what it took.
Nux pulled the vampire into his embrace, placing her head on his chest as he rubbed her back, assuring her that he was here, right next to her.
Then, he closed his eyes as well, remembering the words his father-in-law said just to
him before he disappeared.
'Protect her!
Nux frowned at those words.
something happened, he wouldn't care about Yrniel any longer and would appear next
to her that very instant.
Then why would he...
'I wouldn't be able to wake up on my own unless Yrniel's Will wakes me up when it
senses danger.
If something happens to her, I probably won't be there.
So I'll be leaving her to you!
'What...? Then why are you sending her with me?"
Nux couldn't help but question. After all, he knew this man would usually never put his
daughter at risk and he completely understood that feeling. After all, he would never put his wives in danger either, no matter what.
Azriel was similar to him when it came to this, then why...
'I do not want her to be lonely!
Nux suddenly heard the answer to his question and when he turned to look at his
father-in-law, he had disappeared.

Some, left without a family and with limited time, even decided to teach their family's cultivation techniques to mortals.
It was a day that would bring forth an entirely new generation of cultivators.
"He is gone..."
However, not everyone was happy.
Aeliana, who was observing the changes in Yrniel and the dimensions connected to it,
realized that her father had returned to his slumber again.
Once again, she would have to live a life without her father next to her.
"Don't worry, we will wake him up soon enough, I promise."
Suddenly, the woman heard some reassuring words as she felt someone holding her
hand.
Knowing who it was, she tightened her grip on his hand and closed her eyes.
Her heavy heart eased a little.
After all, she knew these weren't empty words.
This man had set everything right and changed her life before.
Aeliana knew he would do it again, no matter what it took.
Nux pulled the vampire into his embrace, placing her head on his chest as he rubbed her back, assuring her that he was here, right next to her.
Then, he closed his eyes as well, remembering the words his father-in-law said just to
him before he disappeared.
'Protect her!
Nux frowned at those words.
something happened, he wouldn't care about Yrniel any longer and would appear next
to her that very instant.
Then why would he...
'I wouldn't be able to wake up on my own unless Yrniel's Will wakes me up when it
senses danger.
If something happens to her, I probably won't be there.
So I'll be leaving her to you!
'What...?
Then why are you sending her with me?"
Nux couldn't help but question.
After all, he knew this man would usually never put his
daughter at risk and he completely understood that feeling.
After all, he would never put his wives in danger either, no matter what.
Azriel was similar to him when it came to this, then why...
'I do not want her to be lonely!
Nux suddenly heard the answer to his question and when he turned to look at his
father-in-law, he had disappeared.

chapters.title: Chapter 1825 Mission: Crush Tandris
paragraphs: 'I do not want her to be lonely!
These words echoed in Nux's mind as he recalled his memories, and he couldn't help but respect this man-this time, not because of how strong he was, but because of how much he loved his daughter.

If Aeliana stays in Yrniel, let alone killing her, even harming her was next to impossible. She would always be under Azriel's care, and Yrniel would instantly wake Azriel up the moment something happened to Acliana.

If she stays in Yrniel, Azriel would never have to worry about her safety since everything would be in his own hands, but even then, instead of thinking about her safety and being in control, he decided to let go of having control and left his treasured daughter to a man far, far weaker than him.
Nux didn't know if he was capable of doing that.
He knew how scary loneliness was-heck, he had experienced it for a million years and had pretty much lost his mind-but even after knowing what he knew,
He highly doubted he would grow the willpower to compromise the safety of the ones he loved.
'I have so much room to grow...
Nux couldn't help but think inwardly.
'Nux
Then suddenly, he heard a voice.
'Hm?'
'Astaria got the mission.
Felberta informed, and Nux's smile widened.
"Let's get ready."
He spoke out loud.
"Where?"
Aeliana questioned.
"Core."
"Alright." Aeliana nodded.
Nux then opened the portal, and the two walked into the Core, where the rest of the women, who Nux had severed, along with Eisheth and Vulpiana, were present.
"Hey hey hey, let me read it as well."
Edda spoke excitedly as she reached Astaria, who had the mission details in her hand. "Why are you, out of all people, so excited?" Ember couldn't help but question.
"Heh. Who knows? My dream might finally come true."
Edda laughed mysteriously, and the rest of the women stared at her as if they were staring at a madwoman.
After all, they knew what this woman's 'dream' was. There was no 'mystery' here. "Give it to me."
Ember just extended her hand, and Astaria passed the details to her. The rest of the women all surrounded Ember and started reading as well,
Mission: Crush Tandris
Mission Description:

The war between Velcria and Tandris has continued for hundreds of years. The World's Will plays a crucial role in this conflict, granting its natives significant advantages when fighting on their home world. This makes invasions costly and inefficient, leading to a prolonged stalemate. Velcria, desperate to break this deadlock, has turned to clite mercenaries to ensure their victory.
Mission Objective:
The mercenaries are tasked with leading the Velcrian forces to victory by:
Conquering Tandris's Capital, Draventhis. Crippling Tandris's ability to retaliate and forcing unconditional surrender.
Important Points:

World's Will Detection: The moment mercenaries enter Tandris, the World's Will will inform Tandris's leadership of their arrival and provide their live locations. Stealth and infiltration are impossible.
Natives' Advantage: Velcrian forces will be weakened since they won't be in their home world. Tandris's defenders will be much more powerful because of the Tandris's Will supporting them.
No Direct Assistance: The factions the two worlds are part of will not intervene directly; mercenaries are to rely on their own skills, tactics, and the Velcrian forces.
Desired Outcome of the Mission:

Velcria's Victory: The fall of Draventhis marks the end of the war. Tandris's leadership surrenders, and Velcria claims dominance over the enemy world. Once they win, Velcrian forces can be used as reinforcements by their faction, and Velcria's status in their faction would rise.
Rewards:
1 Million Mercenary Points.
Bonus Rewards:
Relics, Treasures, and Artifacts recovered from Draventhis (Conditions applied).
Permanent status as elite partners of Velcria's ruling council, granting access to exclusive contracts, missions, and resources.
Reputation: Successfully completing this mission will cement your mercenary party's reputation as legends capable of turning the tide of world-shaping conflicts.
"Woah..."
Edda couldn't help but voice her amazement. It wasn't just her; the rest of the women
were taken aback as well,
"This... is much grander than I thought."
Rune commented, and Thyra nodded with a solemn look on her face.
"I thought the mission would be enlisting into a world's army as soldiers and then
continuing from there."
Melia muttered, and the others nodded.
"Mhm, this one looks like all the control is given to us." Aisha nodded.
"There were missions where we were enlisted into armies; those missions were from middle-level worlds. There were even some from low-level worlds, but the rewards
were low."
Astaria answered.
"Rewards?" Allura frowned.
After all, the last thing they cared about was rewards.
"Reputation."
Astaria clarified.

"Even if we are now Elite Mercenaries, we aren't the best. Yes, we can take any missions we want; however, the elite missions are different from normal missions. In these missions, the one who enlisted them can decide whether they want a certain
party on their mission or not.
Our party's reputation only extends to our mercenary world. In the other mercenary worlds, we are nothing but a nameless party.
There are chances we might get rejected by the party that enlisted the mission. This is also the reason it takes a few days to accept elite missions; it doesn't get accepted
until the enlisting party approves of us.
Actually, before this, our party was rejected two times."
"We were rejected...?"
Ember blinked.
"Mhm."
Astaria.
"The only reason Velcria accepted us was because we never failed even a single
mission till now.
Also, the rumors of us annihilating that Titan's Party might have had a hand in it as
well."
"The rumors spread that far?"
Allura was surprised.
"Well, they are in a pinch, so it wouldn't be a surprise if they do their research."
Astaria shrugged.
"But still...
We were rejected...
That too, in a Mission related to a War."
Ember spoke in a low voice.
"I guess we need to make a name for ourselves in this mission to make sure that𝚏𝕣𝐞𝗲𝐰𝕖𝐛𝐧𝕠𝕧𝚎𝚕.𝐜𝚘𝗺
doesn't happen again, no?"
Astaria grinned, then her grin widened even further and,
"Also, Nux said we do not need to hold back any longer.
So... my fellow Leanders, go all out."
The swordswoman then glanced at the dragon and,
"We will be relying on you, General."

chapters.title: Chapter 1826 It’s a strange name.
paragraphs: "So... you are the party 'the ones who actually do all the work and should be rewarded' that took the mission we posted?"
A 1.2-meter tall, slender humanoid being with leaf-colored hair, long ears, vine-covered limbs, and green-tinted skin questioned as she raised her eyebrow.
Her eyes resembled blooming flowers, and according to common knowledge, those eyes shifted colors according to the woman's mood.
'So she is a Sylvanix?'
Edda questioned, using the Harem Seal's connection. Yes!
Thyra nodded.
Before coming to Velcria, the women had done their research, so they knew what to expect.
'She is so cute-'
Skyla muttered, her eyes shimmering brightly as she stared at the woman in front of her.
"Yes,"
Ember nodded.
Since this was related to war, the Dragon had taken command.
She extended her hand forward, wanting to complete the introductions, but suddenly, "It's a strange name."
The Sylvanix spoke without hesitation.
"We had our reasons."
Ember answered.
"I do not know what 'reason' would make you use such a comical name. It is almost as if all of this is a joke to you, I cannot leave the fate of my world to people who cannot take things seriously."

The Sylvanix spoke with a cold look on her face, the color of her eyes turning icy blue. "We didn't force you to accept our application. You chose us yourself, and I am sure you didn't choose us based on our names.
People who cannot take things seriously?
Does our previous record not tell you anything?
Or are you implying we completed all our missions without a single failure despite not being serious?

If that is indeed the case, I am not surprised that you still haven't won this war. The last thing a leader should be doing is judging others by their names or appearance. I thought those were the basics."
Ember retorted.

It didn't matter if they were only mercenaries; they needed to set things straight here. Yes, they wanted to clear this mission, but it didn't mean they would be subservient. They were doing all this for reputation, to create an image-an image Nux would later use to advance and get closer to the Core of the War. They would not ruin that image at any cost.
"I do not like the way you talk"
The Sylvanix narrowed her eyes.
She wasn't weak; she was one of the leaders of her world. She was a Primordial, and she wouldn't allow any disrespect.
"I only speak the tru-"
Ember wanted to retort, but suddenly,
"Tsk, why are you even wasting your time talking to them? They are clearly weaker than we expected. Just send them away. We need to hire another party,"
A 5-meter-tall being snorted.
The women observed the being silently. Just like the Sylvanix, they knew him as well. A Stoneborn.

Massive, humanoid beings with rocky skin that resembled polished gemstones. Their eyes were like glowing orbs of molten magma. They were known for their incredible durability and were naturally imposing.
Just like the Sylvanix Leader, he was a Primordial as well.
"Weaker than you expected?"
Ember tilted her head as she realized.
"So you knew..."
She muttered aloud.
The Stoneborn narrowed his eyes at those words, and Ember continued,
"You call us weaker than expected when you already knew the strength of our party when we registered to take the mission.
If you still accepted us, then it must mean you heard the rumors about our party
"Clearly, those were merely rumors. I was told that that party had five Primordials, There is no way you lot have the power to take on even one Primordial, let alone five!"𝙧𝙚𝙚𝔀𝒆𝓫𝓷𝙤𝓿𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝙤𝓶
The Stoneborn didn't hide it either.
Hearing his words, Ember smirked.
"So you were hoping to hire a Primordial-level mercenary at the price of a Sovereign?
You are a funny lot."
"Mind your words, woman. Don't make me use force."
The Stoneborn threatened, the ground around his feet rumbling. It was an intimidating sight, or... at least it should have been, but...
"Don't be mistaken, Velcrian.
We are not your subordinates.
We did not come here to assist you in this war. We came here to win it for you.
We came here to do what you and your people couldn't. And we wouldn't have applied for this mission if we weren't confident in our ability to complete it.
You plan on going against a force that believes it could destroy your enemy, who is as strong as you. It is not a smart plan,"
Ember replied, and as she said those words, the rest of the women, even Skyla, glared at the three leaders standing in front of them.

That look on their faces was enough to show their stance, and seeing nine Sovereigns showing such confidence in front of three Primordials and dozens of Sovereign-level guards who were hidden and ready to attack at any moment surprised the Velcrian
Leaders.
Honestly, the Stoneborn Leader was close to losing it.

The Stoneborns were known for their arrogance, impatience, and straightforwardness. The Stoneborn Leader wanted to show these women their place, so he was about to activate his Aura and put these women on their knees. However,
before he could do so,
"Please calm down."
A melodious voice was heard.
The third leader had finally spoken.
She was a Seraphyte.
A humanoid being with glowing, feathered wings and radiant golden eyes. Her hair glimmered with hues of gold, silver, or platinum, and her presence exuded an aura of
calm and tranquility.
These were the beings of light.
While the Stoneborns were known as the protectors of Velcria because of their might,
and the Sylvanix were the caretakers of Velcria's ecosystem, the Seraphytes were
known as its leaders who oversaw everything.
The instant the Seraphyte spoke, the Stoneborn turned silent as if a foreign force had
calmed his mind. The woman then turned toward Ember and extended her hand.
"We got off to an unpleasant start;
Let's begin anew,"

chapters.title: Chapter 1827 We need a plan of attack...
paragraphs: "We got off to an unpleasant start;
Let's begin anew."
The Seraphyte spoke with a light smile on her face. Ember stared at her hand for at moment before she accepted her handshake, making her widen her smile.
"My name is Liora Shineway."
The Seraphyte Leader, Liora, introduced herself. Then, she pointed at the Stoneborn Leader and,
"My friend here is Kaelgran Forgeheart,"
Then finally, she glanced at the Sylvanix and,
"And she is Elaris Bloomveil.
We three are the Leaders of Velcria and we would like to welcome you to our world."
"I am Ember Leander."
Ember introduced herself.
Then, she started introducing her sisters,
"She is Skyla Leander,
Edda Leander,
Allura Leander.
Thyra Leander.
Astaria Leander.
Aisha Leander.
Melia Leander.
And Rune Leander,"
"Leanders, huh..."
Liora noticed the same last name.
"We are sisters. You can call us the Leander Family if you'd prefer."
"I understand."
Liora nodded.
"You do not look like sisters to me."
Elaris spoke with a slight frown on her face, her eyes turning purple.
Che une referring to the different racial features of the women procent in front of her
but.
"We are."
Ember answered dismissively, not wanting to talk more about it.
Elaris didn't poke any further either.
Kaclgran, the Stoneborn, didn't care either way. He was already angry, and if it wasn't for Liora holding him back, he would have attacked these weaklings.
"Hmph."
He snorted as he looked away, clearly not interested in conversation.
"Please do not mind him, he has a fiery temper."
Liora spoke with a wry smile on her face.
"It doesn't matter, my race is known to have a fiery temper as well."
Ember nodded. Her words sounded supportive, but Kaelgran and even Liora could sense her hidden disdain.
Not that Ember was trying to hide it anyway.
A World Leader who couldn't control his emotions?
She was surprised this world survived this long.
'It is probably because they joined the Faction!
Astaria, knowing what her sister might be thinking about, gave her input.
'Mhm.'
Ember nodded back; she had come to the same conclusion.
"Ember, if you do not mind, can I ask a question?"
Liora spoke politely.
"Please ask."
Ember nodded.
"Are the rumors true?"
Ember stared at the Seraphyte, and Liora continued,
"I will be honest,

Yes, you were correct, the reason we accepted your application was because of that rumor. Our informants told us that one of your party members threw the head of a Primordial from that party inside the mercenary hall.
"You investigated so far, yet you still weren't able to find out whether the rumor is true or not?"
Ember questioned as she raised her eyebrow.
Then, a light smile appeared on her face and,
"Or is it that you dare not believe what you were told?"
"Where I stand, I would want that to be nothing but the truth, but..."
"But?"

paragraphs: Liora spoke.
"I have a plan."
Ember nodded and,
"Attack."
Kaelgran frowned.
"What does that mean?"
He questioned.
Ember stared at him and,
"You have an army that is as strong as theirs, no?"
"Our army is stronger than them. They only survive because they hide in their world."
Kaelgran was quick to add his point.
"That makes it easier."
Ember nodded.
"We will go for an all-out war and take over their capital in two days."
"What?"
Elaris blinked in surprise.
"Without a plan...?"
Liora frowned.
"What plan do you need?"
Ember questioned.
"You do not expect me to leave the fate of my world on your whims, do you? Your words alone aren't very reassuring for me."
Liora was honest.
And Ember understood her point.
To her, they were nothing more than strangers, and their cultivation levels weren't very reassuring either.
Even Ember, if stuck in Liora's place, wouldn't believe them.
"Tell me shout vaur army"
Ember asked with a solemn look on her face.
Liora tilted her head and Ember continued,
"My Law allows me to strengthen the army I lead. Tell me about your army, and I will tell you how much I can strengthen it. I believe that will give you a form of assurance and build trust."
Liora stared at Ember for a while, and then, she nodded.
"Veleria has a million-man strong army.
Our army is divided into three forces.
The Sylvanix Forces, or the Verdant Vanguard.
The total number of Sylvanix soldiers in our army is 350,000 soldiers.
The Sylvanix, because of their abilities, specialize in precision, stealth, and magical combat.
These soldiers utilize their deep connection to nature to deploy plant-based magic to manipulate terrain, entangle enemies, and strengthen their defenses with living fortifications.
In the Sylvanix Force, there exists an elite unit made up of the strongest Sylvanix Sovereigns, called the Bloom Wardens.
The Bloom Wardens can unleash catastrophic environmental magic, such as creating impenetrable vine mazes or summoning giant, animated trees as guardians.
Their mastery of guerrilla warfare tactics ensures that they can strike swiftly and vanish without a trace.
They are ideal for ambushes and attrition strategies.
The second force in our army is the Stoneborn Forces, or the Granite Legion, with 400,000 soldiers.
They have high durability, brute strength, and are good at siege warfare.
The Stoneborn warriors are the bulwark of Veleria's army.
Their gemstone-like skin acts as natural armor, making them nigh-indestructible in battle.
These beings wield giant weapons capable of leveling enemy fortifications or destroying enemy formations with a single swing.
The Stoneborn Elite Unit, which consists of strong Sovereign Level Stoneborns, is
called the Earthshapers.
They can manipulate the battlefield, erecting stone walls, creating pits to trap enemies, or summoning devastating localized earthquakes.
which are unmatched in durability and destructive power. These siege engines ensure
swift assaults on fortified positions.
The final one of the three forces is the Seraphyte Forces, or the Radiant Host.
There are 250,000 of them.
Because of their wings, they specialize in flight, mobility, support magic, and celestial
combat.
Seraphytes bring unmatched grace and strategic brilliance to Velcria's army.
With their wings, they dominate the skies, raining attacks or providing aerial support
to ground forces.
Their abilities enable them to heal wounded soldiers, create blinding flashes to disorient enemies, or forge luminous weapons and shields for battle.
Their elite unit, the Aetherblades, are masters of aerial combat, combining speed with devastating precision.
These three forces are trained together to bring out the best from each of them.
Their differing strengths and abilities help them work in perfect harmony.
The Sylvanix manipulate the battlefield with their environmental magic, creating natural barriers and controlling enemy movements.
The Stoneborn hold the frontlines, serving as an impenetrable shield against enemy
assaults.
And the Seraphytes dominate the skies, supporting both ground and aerial operations with their light-based magic and healing abilities.
Their aura of calm and their leadership skills ensure that the army remains disciplined and resolute, even in the face of overwhelming odds.
In total, there are 300,000 Sovereigns, out of which the elite units of the three forces have 20,000 Sovereigns each.
Other soldiers have still not formed their Laws yet. Some, however, have formed their Paths and are stronger than the others.
There are also reserved forces, but they specialize in defense and only move when Velcria is invaded."
Liora gave a brief description, and Ember nodded.
She could tell that the Seraphyte was hiding quite a lot of things, but it didn't matter.
She wasn't expecting a World Leader to be completely open about their forces to a
foreign mercenary party.
No sane leader would do that.
"SA
You have a million soldiers in your army,
300,000 of which are Sovereigns and 700,000 are Saints and Semi-Saints, correct?"
"Saints and Semi-Saints?"
Liora frowned.
"Ah, I meant the Protectors."
"Yes. 700,000 are at the Protector Stage."
Liora affirmed.
"That's stronger than I thought!'
Astaria muttered.
All these were complete cultivators. This army was much stronger than Yrniel's if we
take out the Progenitors.
"This is what the influence of an Outer World does to a world, huh...? It pushes the
people to their limits!
Melia muttered.
'It might also be because they are a part of a faction!
Rune gave her input.
'It doesn't matter. We should just assume that the enemy forces are as strong as theirs.
Ember, how much can you strengthen them?'
Thyra questioned, and instead of answering her, Ember stared at the Seraphyte and,
"If you allow me to command your army,
then, considering that the enemy forces are as strong as yours, I give you my word
that even with the enemy forces being strengthened by their World's Will, I'll win this
war with less than 250,000 casualties."
"What...?"
Liora's expression changed.
"Less than... 250,000 casualties...? How...?"
"As I said, my Law allows me to strengthen my army. The higher the number of
soldiers in my army, the greater the effect of my Law.
With your million-strong army, I can strengthen your Protectors to be able to survive
against a Low-Level Sovereign.
I will boost their strength to the level where if around five High-Level Protectors worked together, they would be able to take one Low-Level Sovereign."

chapters.title: Chapter 1829 A demonstration would help quite a bit.
paragraphs: "As I said, my Law allows me to strengthen my Army. The higher the number of soldiers in my army, the greater the effect of my Law.

With your million-strong army, I can strengthen your Protectors to be able to survive against a Low-Level Sovereign. I will boost their strength to the level where, if around five High-Level Protectors worked together, they would be able to take one Low-Level Sovereign."
Ember spoke, and she wasn't done yet.
"Think about it:
Every single Low-Level Protector of your army would be able to take on even a High-Level Protector.
Every five I ligh-Level Protectors of your army would be able to fight a Low-Level enemy Sovereign.
Every Low-Level Sovereign of your army would be able to take on a High-Level enemy Sovereign.
As for the High-Level Sovereigns, under my commands, as long as a Primordial doesn't step in front of them, they will be unstoppable-able to take on even multiple Sovereigns at the same time.

Honestly, when I say there will only be 250,000 casualties, I am considering the worst-case scenario: where the enemy has a trump card none of us know about, a highly advanced bomb, weapons made by a high-level blacksmith, or something else.

I am talking about the case where the enemy highly outclasses you in any way possible. However, if the enemy's strength is as you say, then with my Law, I doubt there would be more than 50,000 deaths.
But to do that, what I need is for your army to surrender to me. For my Law to work, I need every single soldier in your army to accept me as their Leader-the Army General with Absolute Command."
Those were heavy conditions. Leaving the command of their army to a woman they met just a few minutes ago was an absurd notion.
A notion the Velcria Leaders would have rejected in an instant if the conditions Ember presented in return weren't so absurd.
A victory with less than 50,000 casualties?
All of it honestly felt like a fantasy that none of the leaders could believe.
"Stop the bullshit," the Stoneborn Leader, Kaelgran, snorted out loud.
"Your Law allows you to strengthen your Army? Do you even realize how absurd that
sounds? Are you telling us to believe that you are a war resource that can turn around any war's scenario just with your mere presence?"
Kaelgran's tone was extremely condescending, and while they didn't say it out loud, it was clear that Liora and Elaris thought the same.
Of course, the way Liora worded it was much more... leader-like.
"If you have such a Law, I assume you have experience in leading soldiers?" Liora spoke as she stared at Ember.
"I do." Ember nodded confidently.
"Then you, out of all people, should know that the soldiers won't treat you like a true general just because we tell them to.
The soldiers are not mindless robots who would do anything they were told to. They would have questions, they would have doubts.
They would need reason to fully trust you, they would need reason to put their lives in your hands and do what you tell them to.
And the only person who can create such trust would be...
You."
Hearing her words, Ember's grin widened.
'I knew she was the smarter one out of the three, Thyra commented.
'Mhm, she is indeed.' Rune nodded as well.
'I have no clue why that talking rock is in this room! Aisha chuckled.
'It's because he is strong!
Astaria's answer was quick.
'But he is also dumb.
'It doesn't matter. He is still a Primordial.
The women just shrugged.
Ember, on the other hand, nodded at Liora.
"I understand.
How about you gather your army, and I will try to gain their trust. If I succeed, I will become their Leader. If I don't, well...
Then you can declare this mission to be a failure and hire some other mercenary
party."
"Are you going to stain your otherwise perfect record?" Elaris raised her eyebrow.
"Who said I am going to fail?" Ember chuckled.
"I like your confidence." Elaris nodded with a smile.
The Sylvanix Leader started liking this woman despite their bad start.
"Thank you, Lady Elaris." Ember bowed lightly.𝙛𝒓𝓮𝒆𝔀𝒆𝙗𝓷𝒐𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝓶
"How about this? There are nine of you, correct?
We will gather nine of our strongest Sovereigns, and you all will face them in a group
battle with you as your party's Leader.
It will be a good demonstration of your strength and your Law.
If we do this in front of our army, and if you people win, you might win the soldiers'
trust." Elaris suggested.
Ember, however, shook her head, rejecting her idea.
"That would be too unfair."
"Heeh? Weren't you confident about winning even against Primordials just now?
Chickening out already?" Kaelgran questioned with a wide grin on his face. Clearly, he was mocking Ember,
Ember, however, remained emotionless and,
"I was talking about your soldiers.
A battle against us would be too unfair for them.
We would win even if I do not use my Law."
Ember declared confidently.
"It won't prove anything, so let's not waste time."
Ember wanted to continue, but,
"No, please, I insist."
Kaelgran interrupted.
He had had enough of this woman's arrogance.
That proud tone of hers, he didn't like it one bit.
Therefore,
"I want you to fight our strongest soldiers. I assure you, it would have a great effect on
our soldiers.
It would also help us introduce you with more ease." Kaelgran spoke; his words finally sounded somewhat leader-like.
Ember glanced at Liora, and the Seraphyte nodded as well.
"A demonstration would help quite a bit."
her face, she sighed in defeat.

which was even wider than his.

as nonchalant as the catwoman.

I will boost their strength to the level where, if around five High-Level Protectors worked together, they would be able to take one Low-Level Sovereign."
Ember spoke, and she wasn't done yet.
"Think about it:
Every single Low-Level Protector of your army would be able to take on even a High-Level Protector.
Every five I ligh-Level Protectors of your army would be able to fight a Low-Level enemy Sovereign.
Every Low-Level Sovereign of your army would be able to take on a High-Level enemy Sovereign.
As for the High-Level Sovereigns, under my commands, as long as a Primordial doesn't step in front of them, they will be unstoppable-able to take on even multiple Sovereigns at the same time.

Honestly, when I say there will only be 250,000 casualties, I am considering the worst-case scenario: where the enemy has a trump card none of us know about, a highly advanced bomb, weapons made by a high-level blacksmith, or something else.
I am talking about the case where the enemy highly outclasses you in any way possible.
However, if the enemy's strength is as you say, then with my Law, I doubt there would be more than 50,000 deaths.
But to do that, what I need is for your army to surrender to me.
For my Law to work, I need every single soldier in your army to accept me as their Leader-the Army General with Absolute Command."
Those were heavy conditions.
Leaving the command of their army to a woman they met just a few minutes ago was an absurd notion.
A notion the Velcria Leaders would have rejected in an instant if the conditions Ember presented in return weren't so absurd.
A victory with less than 50,000 casualties?
All of it honestly felt like a fantasy that none of the leaders could believe.
"Stop the bullshit," the Stoneborn Leader, Kaelgran, snorted out loud.
"Your Law allows you to strengthen your Army?
Do you even realize how absurd that
sounds?
Are you telling us to believe that you are a war resource that can turn around any war's scenario just with your mere presence?"
Kaelgran's tone was extremely condescending, and while they didn't say it out loud, it was clear that Liora and Elaris thought the same.
Of course, the way Liora worded it was much more... leader-like.
"If you have such a Law, I assume you have experience in leading soldiers?" Liora spoke as she stared at Ember.
"I do." Ember nodded confidently.
"Then you, out of all people, should know that the soldiers won't treat you like a true general just because we tell them to.
The soldiers are not mindless robots who would do anything they were told to.
They would have questions, they would have doubts.
They would need reason to fully trust you, they would need reason to put their lives in your hands and do what you tell them to.
And the only person who can create such trust would be...
You."
Hearing her words, Ember's grin widened.
'I knew she was the smarter one out of the three, Thyra commented.
'Mhm, she is indeed.' Rune nodded as well.
'I have no clue why that talking rock is in this room!
Aisha chuckled.
'It's because he is strong!
Astaria's answer was quick.
'But he is also dumb.
'It doesn't matter.
He is still a Primordial.
The women just shrugged.
Ember, on the other hand, nodded at Liora.
"I understand.
How about you gather your army, and I will try to gain their trust.
If I succeed, I will become their Leader.
If I don't, well...
Then you can declare this mission to be a failure and hire some other mercenary
party."
"Are you going to stain your otherwise perfect record?" Elaris raised her eyebrow.
"Who said I am going to fail?" Ember chuckled.
"I like your confidence." Elaris nodded with a smile.
The Sylvanix Leader started liking this woman despite their bad start.
"Thank you, Lady Elaris." Ember bowed lightly.𝙛𝒓𝓮𝒆𝔀𝒆𝙗𝓷𝒐𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝓶
"How about this?
There are nine of you, correct?
We will gather nine of our strongest Sovereigns, and you all will face them in a group
battle with you as your party's Leader.
It will be a good demonstration of your strength and your Law.
If we do this in front of our army, and if you people win, you might win the soldiers'
trust." Elaris suggested.
Ember, however, shook her head, rejecting her idea.
"That would be too unfair."
"Heeh?
Weren't you confident about winning even against Primordials just now?
Chickening out already?" Kaelgran questioned with a wide grin on his face.
Clearly, he was mocking Ember,
Ember, however, remained emotionless and,
"I was talking about your soldiers.
A battle against us would be too unfair for them.
We would win even if I do not use my Law."
Ember declared confidently.
"It won't prove anything, so let's not waste time."
Ember wanted to continue, but,
"No, please, I insist."
Kaelgran interrupted.
He had had enough of this woman's arrogance.
That proud tone of hers, he didn't like it one bit.
Therefore,
"I want you to fight our strongest soldiers.
I assure you, it would have a great effect on
our soldiers.
It would also help us introduce you with more ease." Kaelgran spoke; his words finally sounded somewhat leader-like.
Ember glanced at Liora, and the Seraphyte nodded as well.
"A demonstration would help quite a bit."
her face, she sighed in defeat.
"Alright, we accept."
Kaelgran's grin widened.
What he completely missed was the grin on Astaria's face,
which was even wider than his.
Soon, however, Astaria's grin disappeared as Ember laid out her commands.
'Rune, you will be taking on all nine of them.'
'Okay!
Rune nodded, not putting much thought into it.
However, not every person was
as nonchalant as the catwoman.
'What!?
Why!?
It's clear that they want all of us to fight because they want to see our strength!
And Nux told us not to hold back anymore; it is a perfect opportu-
'Astaria, I do not plan to kill them.
The last person I want those poor soldiers to face is you.
Ember spoke, and before
Astaria could retort,
'I agree!
Thyra nodded.
'Me too."
'Mhm, she cannot be allowed to go all out!
Yup, too monstrous!
The rest of the women nodded, agreeing with their General's decision.
'Sister Star...
I am sorry, but I am on Sister Ember's side today...'

chapters.title: Chapter 1830 Rune’s Strength.
paragraphs: "Let's end it here, shall we?"

Rune spoke casually with an expressionless look on her face as she sat on top of a 6-meter large Stoneborn, pointing her dagger at the giant gemstone protruding from the center of his giant, stony back.
The Stoneborn didn't answer. He was currently lying on the ground, his eyes looking at the 'battlefield'

There were dead vines all over the place, trying to capture or attack this cat. Some of these vines were also burned or crushed. However, none of the damage to these vines was done by the woman sitting on his back.
The vines were crushed by his allies instead.
As for the woman, she didn't have to attack these vines. For some reason, every time any Sylvanix tried to target her using their vines, it never worked.
She always dodged their attacks with absolute precision. Her movements were so fast that none of them were able to see through them.
It wasn't just the Sylvanix who failed to attack her. The Seraphytes and even Stoneborns, known for their strength, couldn't attack her.
She was like a slippery eel that no one could catch, no matter what they did.
Even if his team tried to use wide-range attacks, she would disappear and never get hurt. It was as if she could read their minds and knew exactly what they were going to do.
From start to finish, the woman never even attacked. She just appeared next to her target, placed her dagger at their vital point, and forced them to admit defeat without hurting any of them.
And no, it wasn't merciful.
It was humiliating.

For the nine strongest Sovereigns of Velcria, each being a member of the Elite Unit of their respective forces and having exceptional teamwork that covered each other's weak points, to lose to an opponent in such a humiliating manner...
It made them tremble in shame.
It felt like the opponent was on a light stroll. There was not even a single drop of sweat on her face.
And what's worse?
This woman defeated all nine of them, alone.
Yes, it was just this small woman who defeated the strongest of Velcria. The rest of her 'team' didn't even move.
Even now, they were all sitting on the chairs that they had taken out, looking at the scene in front of them with calm looks on their faces.
It was as if they were already expecting such a result, and this didn't surprise them one bit.
Seeing the looks on their faces enraged the Stoneborn even further.
"No! I do not admit defeat!"
The Stoneborn screamed in rage as he tried to use this chance, when the woman had dropped her guard, thinking she had won, to grab her and eliminate her from the
battle.
Yes, it was a cowardly method. However, the Stoneborn wanted to face the rest of the
women.
Even if one of them stood up, it would be enough.
He wanted to see, he wanted to know what this monstrous bunch was made of.
He, however, couldn't fulfill his wish, as his hand could only grasp air.
The woman sitting on top of his back had already moved away.
"There is no point to continue the battle."
The Stoneborn heard the woman's voice again.
"I SAID I DIDN'T LOSE!!"
BOOM
He screamed as he slammed his giant arms on the ground and stood up.
The ground beneath him cracked, and dust moved in all directions, hindering people's
vision.
The Stoneborn stepped forward. He knew staying in an area with low vision against an agile opponent would put him at a disadvantage, but then...
As he moved forward, his right knee suddenly collapsed as he was attacked from behind, forcing him to kneel.
He moved his hand, trying to slam away the woman, but again, the woman had already moved away and attacked his other knee, making him lose his balance and fall to the
ground again.
Knowing what happened was going to repeat itself, the man stopped himself from falling, trying to fly away and gain distance, but...
"This should be enough. You even got a second chance."
He heard the woman's voice again.
The Stoneborn realized that the woman was sitting cross-legged on top of him, her dagger pointing at his weakness again.
The only difference was that this time, he was floating in the air instead of being on
the ground.
BOOOM
He screamed as he rotated and crashed onto the ground, crushing the woman beneath his giant body.
With his weight, not many could survive this attack. He had even used his ability to somewhat alter his body, making it difficult for the woman to escape in time.
The speed at which all of this was done was so fast that barely a few beings in this world would be able to react to it.
And even if they did, by the time they acted, they would already be crushed under his
weight.
However...
As the dust cleared up and the Stoneborn came back to his senses, he could sense that there was no one underneath him.
This attack... it was nothing more than him crashing onto the ground and rolling in
the mud, by himself.
Step Step Step
The Stoneborn then heard footsteps approaching him. He could tell that the woman
was doing this on purpose.
It was her way of telling him that his attack didn't do anything... yet again.
"How long ar-"
"I WILL DESTROY YOU!!!"
He screamed as he stood up and rushed towards Rune.
The cat woman prepared to dodge, but then,
BOOOOOOM
A horrifying pressure descended, enveloping the Stoneborn's body and pushing him to
the ground.
The pressure wasn't even aimed at Rune, but for a fleeting moment, her knees
wobbled.
Even she, who had been untouchable in the battle, couldn't resist this force and was about to fall to her knees.
However, before that could happen, her shadow trembled, and the pressure that seemed too strong to resist became ineffective on her, as if it was canceled out.
Seeing that, a light smile appeared on Rune's indifferent face.
She looked down. There, she saw her shadow making a thumbs-up and a heart sign. Then, it winked at her, making her chuckle out loud.

chapters.title: Chapter 1831 My name is Ember Leander
paragraphs: 'Nux, you said you won't interfere!
Rune chuckled out loud as she saw her shadow acting like that.
"What? I am just supporting my lovely wife
I wouldn't have interfered if the one who attacked you were your opponents.
A Primordial doesn't count.
Also, I only like my wives on their knees in one situation-'
Nux replied. Once again, Rune's shadow winked at her, making her laugh out loud.
An extremely beautiful smile appeared on Rune's indifferent face. t was a privilege that only Nux could enjoy, and he was doing exactly that.
'My wife is so beautiful-'
He muttered, making Rune smile even more.

Yes, all this while, Nux was inside the women's shadow. This was also the reason these women were confident even in front of the Primordials. After all, they knew the moment these people did something foolish, the one who wins this war would be Tandris.
Rune chuckled again as she then glanced at her opponent. Once again, her face became indifferent.
Her opponent was now crushed to the ground, unable to move even a little. Rune then glanced at the source of the sudden 'pressure!' It was Kaelgran.
"Have you not humiliated us enough already?"

Kaelgran's cold voice was heard as he looked down at his son. Yes, the man Rune was facing was none other than Kaelgran's son, and seeing his own son display such humiliating actions angered Kaelgran. It was one thing to be defeated in a battle, but to not accept that defeat and constantly challenge the opponent while they showed mercy...
Kaelgran couldn't accept such behavior.
Honestly, he wanted nothing more than to crush this fool using his pressure, but, "Hold yourself back, Kaelgran."
Liora ordered, making the Stoneborn take a step back. The pressure he had released disappeared. His son, however, still didn't move. He had passed out.
And this marked the end of the battle between the nine mercenaries and the nine strongest Velcria warriors.
The result? Valorin's humiliating defent

This battle was being broadcast to all of Velcria's soldiers through Velcrian artifacts. When Velcrian soldiers first learned of this arrangement, they thought it was an entertainment show their leaders had arranged for them. A show where they would see their comrades crush a few arrogant mercenaries. After all, how were some mere mercenaries supposed to go against their strongest warriors? Not to mention they were currently in Velcria, their home world, where they are at their strongest. These mercenaries were in for a tough beating.
All the soldiers were excited to see the show, but now...
Silence.
Absolute silence spread all over the place.
Across the barracks, soldiers exchanged uneasy glances. Their pride in Velcria's might was shattered.
The sight of that woman standing amidst the middle of the battlefield haunted their thoughts.

The woman, who had now become the center of attention, turned around and walked towards her sisters. Her sisters nodded at her, except for the auburn-haired woman, who had hugged her out of nowhere. None of them showed much excitement.
Then suddenly, a black-red-haired woman with black-red horns on her head stood up, staring at their Leaders.
One of their Leaders, Liora, sighed, as if admitting her defeat.
"You were correct, it was an unfair battle."
Even a child could see the difference between the two sides.
"I had no reason to lie to you, Lady Liora. We came here to complete the mission; lying would not help with that."
Ember replied.
"Can I talk to your soldiers now?"
Ember questioned.
"Yes, the broadcasting is still active. You can continue."
Liora gave her permission. Ember nodded and then started floating in the air. Soon, she...
Soon, Ember Leander was hovering in the air. All the soldiers focused on her, and she then stared at them through the screen.
My name is Ember Leander, Leader of the Mercenary Party tasked with ending this long war and ensuring your victory.
I know what you're thinking,
How can mere Sovereigns make any difference?
I assure you, we can.
I can.

My Law is unlike anything you have seen. It allows me to strengthen those who follow me with unwavering loyalty. Pledge yourselves to me, and I vow to bring this war to a decisive end-within two days.
I understand that trust cannot be demanded; it must be earned. So I will prove my
worth.

Here is my challenge: your leaders will select 200,000 Protector-level soldiers and divide them into two equal forces of identical strength. One will fight under my command; the other, under a leader of your choice.
When these two supposedly equal forces clash, you will see
The difference my power can make.
The difference my presence alone can make.
with your own eyes.
Yes, this will be a demonstration of my power and what I can do, what your future
Leader can do.
And trust me when I say this, what you will see here would be nothing compared to what will happen in the actual War.
Keep in mind, the effect of my Law depends on the number of people who follow me.
The higher the number, the greater the effects."
Ember then glanced at the soldiers, and then, she smiled.
"So be prepared, soldiers.
Be prepared to see the might of your future leader and the difference she can make."
Ember's words echoed throughout the place. The soldiers stared at each other with unsure looks on their faces. What they heard was too hard to believe.
How could one person make such a big difference?
Normally, they would have dismissed her as a crazy woman, but right now... after
seeing that monstrous woman's might...
They couldn't.
The silence lingered until Ember's gaze shifted to Liora. The leader of Velcria met her
eyes, her expression conflicted but resolute.
She gave Ember a subtle nod before turning to address her people.
"The Protectors who wish to participate in this challenge, step forward."
She spoke, then, with a solemn look on her face, she added.
"My people, keep this in mind as you decide,
The fate of Veleria is on the line here."
Her solemn words sent a ripple through the crowd. The hesitation among the soldiers
was visible, but soon, one soldier stepped forward. Then another. And another.
And soon, 200,000 Soldiers stood in front of Ember and Liora.

chapters.title: Chapter 1832 Let’s do this, shall we?
paragraphs: Liora divided the 200,000 soldiers into two equal forces. To ensure fairness, Ember allowed the enemy leader, who was a Peak Sovereign Stage being and one of the strongest of Velcria, to choose any of the two forces first, and she would take the other one.
An offer the enemy leader accepted.
"...Do you think her ability is as strong as she says?"

Elaris, the Sylvanix Leader, questioned with a doubtful look on her face as she glanced at the other two leaders, mainly at Liora. She wasn't expecting a normal answer from Kaclgran; the Stoneborn wasn't thinking clearly today and seemed agitated for some
reason.
"We will fin-"
"It will."

"Those women are much stronger than we thought."

"Do you remember when I used my Aura to suppress Granson, my son?"

"That girl was near Granson when I used my Aura. Even if I didn't intentionally target her, she should have still felt the suppression from my Law of Self.
At the very least, she should have fallen on her knees if not directly collapsed on the ground like Granson did.
But...
My Aura didn't even faze her.
That woman didn't even renot to it
"What...?"
Liora couldn't believe what she was hearing.
"A Sovereign didn't even react to a Primordial's Aura...?"
"How is that possible...?"
Elaris blinked in disbelief.

Kaelgran, however, had no answer to this question and simply stared at the scene unfolding in front of him, not even wanting to think about what happened before. Especially not the time where he was antagonizing these women...
"Soldiers of Velcria,
You have taken the first step toward something extraordinary.
In this moment, you are not just soldiers-you are pioneers.
The vanguard of change.
The vanguard of victory.
You are the proof of Velcria's resolve.
I am not sugar-coating this; you might think the task before us is monumental, but if you follow me, you would barely need a few hours to end this all."
Ember, still hovering in the air, glanced at the 100,000 soldiers who had come to her side and started addressing them.
For her Law to activate, she needed loyalty. It wouldn't work just because she had soldiers on her side. Ember needed to connect with these soldiers and make them accept her as their leader.
'You know... this would be much simpler if she uses a Slave Seal...'
Aisha couldn't help but speak, finding all of this exhausting.
You think they would allow that?"
Thyra questioned.
"If we ask them nicely, maybe?"
Aisha tilted her head.
'Nicely?
We wish to enslave your soldiers, pretty please-
Do you think that works?'

Let us momentarily enslave your soldiers, and we will end the war with minimal
casualties.

it would all be momentary. Once Ember's Law shows its might, these people would
submit on their own.
The Slave Seal won't be needed.
Aisha's words were convincing.
However,
'She won't do that unless necessary!
Astaria shook her head.

'She is a General. She knows how to connect with the soldiers. Taking command isn't
new for her.
Give her time and let her do what she wants.
This is the place where she shines the brightest.
The rest of the women stared at Ember and nodded with light smiles on their faces.
"I understand you may still harbor doubts about me.
You've served under other leaders, fought countless battles, and endured losses I
cannot even begin to quantify.
But know this: I do not take your loyalty for granted.
I do not see you as numbers to wield or pawns to move.
To me, each one of you is a shield that defends Velcria, a blade that strikes for Velcria's
future, and I intend to bring you together to turn you into an unstoppable force that.
would crush enemies into pieces, overwhelmingly.
My Law strengthens those who follow me, yes, but that is not where my faith lies. My faith lies in you. In your skills, your tenacity, and your unwavering will.
I am not here to replace those qualities but to magnify them.
So today, we will train.
We will prepare.
We will forge ourselves into something your enemies will never anticipate and will
never forget.
Tomorrow, we will show Velcria what it means to stand united, not just in name, but
in spirit and purpose.
This is more than a demonstration.
It is the dawn of something greater.
I have already revealed what my powers can do; the only thing I need is your loyalty.
And now, I demand your loyalty-not for myself, but for Velcria and its future. Pledge yourselves fully, without hesitation, and I will give you the strength to conquer,
Stand with me, and together, we will make history.
Stand with me, and together, we will show the enemies what it means to be a
Velcrian."
Ember then took out her sword and pointed at the force standing in front of her,
"This is the first step.
The step where you help me prove myself and set the foundation for Velcria's victory
against Tandris.
So step forward and,
Crush them."
*BOOOOOOM*
Ember spoke as she then released her overwhelmingly strong Aura.
The soldiers under her command were already motivated by her words. However, the
instant she released her Aura, something within them stirred. Ember's words echoed
in their heads and,

No one knew who screamed at first, but as he did, the rest of the soldiers started
following as well.
"ATTACK!!!"
"YEAHHHHH!!!!"
"FOR VELCRIA!!!"
The soldiers rushed forward.
Ember, who was hovering in the air, felt connected with the soldiers, and the moment
she felt it, a smile appeared on her face.
The Law of Boundless Unity.
It was working. Yes, even now, not all soldiers had truly submitted to her; in fact, most of them had
doubts in their heads.
But it didn't matter.
15,000 out of the 100,000 soldiers had decided to follow her and were now connected
with her through the Law of Boundless Unity.
'Let's do this, shall we?'
Ember chuckled.
I am waiting for you to shine, my Dragon-
The General then heard Nux's voice in her head, and her smile widened even further.
She then raised her hand, activating the Law of Boundless Unity, and,
BOOM BOOM BOOM BOOM
The Aura of those 15,000 soldiers exploded, rising drastically.

chapters.title: Chapter 1833 FOR THE LEADER!!!
paragraphs: Ember then activated the Law of Boundless Unity, and,
BOOM BOOM BOOM BOOM
The Aura of those 15,000 soldiers exploded, rising drastically.
'W-What...?'
"What just happened...?"
The soldiers were surprised, confused as to what was happening to them.
Some soldiers froze mid-charge, their bodies trembling as the power coursed through
them.
Confusion spread like wildfire. Some staggered, their movements disjointed.
Others came to a complete halt, causing those behind them to crash into one another.
The ripple effect of the sudden chaos was instant-and deadly.
The enemy force was closing in.
In an instant, panic, anger, and frustration spread all over Ember's force.
"What's happening!?"
"Why did you stop!?"
"Are you trying to get us killed!?"
"How dare you speak to me like that!?"
"Have you lost your mind!?"
Shouts turned to arguments, and arguments to scuffles. Ember's force was on the verge of imploding.
"Silence."
The single word cut through the chaos like a blade.𝓯𝙧𝓮𝓮𝒘𝓮𝙗𝙣𝒐𝒗𝒆𝓵.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Every soldier turned silent as Ember's voice resonated across the battlefield, carrying an undeniable authority.
"Stand and continue."
Her tone left no room for defiance. Though hesitant and shaken, the soldiers obeyed. The 15,000 soldiers who had received a power boost, however, were still confused. But then,
'Do not worry!
They heard a voice in their heads.
"There is nothing wrong with you.
What you are experiencing is the effect of my Law I told you about.
You people decided to follow me, and this is the reward you have received for taking the brave choice.
You are stronger than before, but keep in mind that being stronger doesn't mean losing your sense of control.

Your task is to target the soldiers you would normally target, then use your greater strength to defeat them quicker than you normally would and help your allies. Remember, you are stronger than before, but you are not allowed to kill them.
They are your allies; I do not want any meaningless deaths.
My Law connects me with all of you,
So I will be keeping an eye on you from a distance,
My soldiers,
I am looking forward to the sight of you dominating the battlefield.
Show them your might
The moment they heard their Leader's voice, all their doubts were cleared. "YEAHHHH!!!!"
"FOR THE LEADER!!!"
With newfound strength and clarity in their eyes, the soldiers rushed toward the enemy force.

Soon, the two supposedly equal forces clashed with each other. At first, everything was just as one would expect-the two leaders stared at each other, the two forces clashed, the soldiers fighting to a standstill.
The enemy leader even wondered if what this woman said was all a lie, and the more this notion settled into his mind, the wider his smile became.
After all, this woman's sister humiliated his World; he could use this chance to avenge his people and become a Hero.
But then,
Something changed.
The soldiers under Ember's command began to move differently. Their strikes were faster, sharper, their defenses impenetrable.
Shields locked together at just the right moments, forming seamless walls of
protection.
Spears thrust forward with unerring precision, exploiting every weakness in the
enemy's lines.
It was as if they shared a single mind, their actions perfectly coordinated.
But this wasn't instinct or luck.
It was her.
'Hold the line on the left.
Rotate and reinforce the gap-yes, now!'
Ember's voice rang out in their heads, clear and commanding despite the chaos.

A group of soldiers grabbed their shields and went into formation. Their shields locked in unison, bracing against the enemy's advance before countering with a precise thrust of their spears. The enemy line faltered, and Ember's soldiers pushed them
back.
'Don't get greedy.
Strike and pull back.
Let the next wave take over-don't break formation!"
Another squad adjusted instantly, their disciplined retreat creating space for fresh soldiers to surge forward. Each motion was fluid, as if rehearsed a thousand times.
'Soldiers at the Front, focus on defense.
Right flank, enemy's line is in the middle of swapping. Use this opening and push forward-don't let them regroup. Move now!"
Her commands were not just orders but guidance, each one landing in her soldiers' minds as if she stood beside them, whispering directly into their ears.
They could feel her presence, steady and unwavering, bolstering their courage and sharpening their focus.
In the chaos of battle, her voice was the lifeline they clung to.
'Stay sharp.
Don't lose sight of your targets.
Strike only when I tell you to!
The soldiers adjusted seamlessly, moving like a single organism. Some had simply stopped using their minds and were following Ember's orders to the letter.
Their fear melted into resolve, doubt transformed into confidence.
In the midst of the chaos, Ember observed the battlefield in silence, analyzing every

single movement with extreme precision. Her thoughts moved faster than any soldier's blade; it was as if time itself had slowed down around her, her commands flowing like a stream, connecting her soldiers in an unbreakable web.
Let alone the soldiers of the enemy force, even the soldiers of her own force that weren't connected to her yet could feel it.
They could see how their comrades were moving differently, they could see how their strength had risen drastically and what kind of impact each and every one of them had
on the battlefield.
These soldiers, who were once their comrades, felt like they were in a league of their
own. They felt... foreign.
'Just... how is this possible...?"
The Soldiers couldn't help but question, and soon, they turned around and glanced at
their leader, who continued to hover in the air, observing the battlefield like a
Goddess.
"They will start pushing harder on the right to try and overwhelm our formation. Intercept them. Others prepare to circle around and flank them.'
What Ember said happened-the opposing force used all their might and attacked from the right, but Ember's soldiers were prepared.
'Now!'
At her orders, the soldiers moved. In an instant, the opposition's formation crumbled.
The tides of the battle were shifting, and they were shifting so fast that the enemy
couldn't react to it.
"What is happening!?"
One of the enemy commanders screamed out loud.
His expression showed his utter disbelief as his soldiers were repelled at every turn.
"They're ordinary soldiers-how are they doing this!?"
"Was the division not equal!? How are their soldiers overpowering ours to this
extent!?"
Another commander questioned out loud.
"No, I know some of those soldiers. They are from my squadron, and they weren't that
strong."
"Then how do you explain that!?"
Another commander shouted as he pointed at the enemy soldiers.
"Do you think ordinary soldiers can move like that!? It is not just their strength; their
movement speed and precision aren't ordinary either! It is as if they were part of special forces and have trained together for centuries!"

paragraphs: "Right now,
She's even stronger than me, let alone that fool.
That fool's running to his death,"
Astaria revealed nonchalantly, and Rune blinked her eyes in disbelief.
"What...?"
Astaria, expecting such a reaction, just turned towards her and smiled.
"What? That woman has the power to make a Semi-Saint defeat a Saint if she has enough numbers.
As long as there is not a difference of an entire Phase between two people, she can strengthen her allies to the point they would become undefeatable. But...
Did you think her allies are the only ones who are strengthened?"
Astaria questioned with a playful smile on her face.
Rune shook her head.
"I know she gets strengthened as well."
"That's an understatement,"
Thyra interrupted.
Rune turned towards her, and Thyra continued,
"The boost that woman gets is stronger than what everyone else gets.
With 100,000 beings under her, no Sovereign here can defeat her.
Well, other than one,"
Thyra spoke as she glanced at her shadow.
Her shadow winked at her, and she just sighed.
"She's that strong? With just 100,000 soldiers under her?"
Rune was shocked,
"Calling her stronger than Astaria might be more of an overstatement, and even you might be able to defeat her right now.
But other than you two, there isn't anyone here who can defeat her,
And it's definitely not him,"
Melia explained more clearly, her eyes on the battlefield.
And just as the women were expecting, as the enemy Sylvanix appeared in front of
Ember, attacking her with a whip he had created out of vines,
The Dragon simply grabbed the whip with her hand, staring at her enemy with an expressionless look on her face.
"W-W-What...?"
The enemy leader couldn't believe it.
Not just him, the soldiers beneath them couldn't believe what they were seeing either.
"You don't want to end up like that stone, do you?"
Ember questioned in an emotionless tone.
Everyone knew what she was talking about, and recalling that humiliation, the enemy leader gritted his teeth.
"Surrender.
It was merely a demonstration,
And now it's over.
You were never supposed to win this thing anyways,"
Ember declared.
Her words were humiliating; however, seeing his position, seeing his soldiers, who had all but surrendered, he knew it was the truth.
Winning was simply impossible because of this woman's existence.
An existence that could change the flow of War with her presence alone.
'Goddess of War...'
The Sylvanix couldn't help but think of these words as he stared at the woman in front of him.
Then, he lowered his head and gave in,
"I surrender."
Ember nodded, and without her having to say it, her soldiers stopped.
"FOR THE LEADER!"
"FOR THE LEADER!"
"FOR THE LEADER!"
The soldiers started chanting, celebrating their victory.
Yes, they were celebrating defeating their own comrades.
Everyone present, including the three Velcria Leaders, stared at these soldiers in silence.
However, before they could say anything, Ember and the other women flew next to
them.
"You did well,"
Liora praised as she glanced at Ember.
"Thank you,"
Ember nodded back respectfully.
"What do you want to do now?"
Liora questioned directly.
She had seen it all-the effect of Ember's Law, her ability to lead soldiers, her ability to
win their trust-she had seen everything with her own eyes.
And if what she said was the truth, then what they saw right now was just the
beginning.
If that was indeed the case, then...
Liora couldn't see Velcria losing this War against Tandris.
Actually, this might very well be the most decisive victory in their history.
It wasn't just Liora. Elaris and even Kaelgran could see it.
A War resource that could turn the tide of any battle with her presence.
Since such an existence stood in front of them, they decided to leave it all to her and
listen to what she says.
Ember smiled and nodded at Liora. Then, she spoke,
"We wait for a week."
"A week? Why?"
Kaelgran questioned.
This time, not because he wanted to oppose these women, but simply because he was
curious.
Also, he was excited to participate in the battle.
The Stoneborn had been holding himself back for a long time now.
"We need to allow the soldiers to talk to each other,"
Ember spoke, and in an instant, the three leaders realized what she wanted.
As the three leaders stared at her, the Dragon nodded.
"If I do what I did today and try to win the soldiers' support in the middle of the War,
there will be pointless casualties. I plan on avoiding that.𝗳𝗿𝐞𝕖𝘄𝗲𝕓𝗻𝚘𝚟𝕖𝐥.𝚌𝕠𝕞
approach the soldiers who were under my command, and once they share what they
experienced today,
It would build trust, making it easier for me to take command in the War."
The three leaders nodded at her words. Ember nodded back and,
"We should dismiss them now."
"Alright."
Liora nodded.
However, before she could say anything,
"Wait,"
Ember interrupted.
"Let me do it,"
She requested.
After Liora nodded, giving her permission, once again, Ember hovered in the air,
attracting the soldiers' attention in an instant.
"Soldiers of Velcria,"
Ember called out.
"What you witnessed today was the strength of Unity.
The strength of your new Leader, your new General.
Yes, I, Ember Leander, have been appointed as your new General, and in one week's
time, we march to War and put an end to this farce.
Tandris, that has been hiding behind its world's will, we are going to destroy it
thoroughly.
Together, we will ensure that Velcria stands unbroken, victorious, and free.
And in this mission, I will stand with you. I will lead you.
And I will not rest until we have won this war.
So prepare yourselves, soldiers of Velcria.
Rest, recover, and return stronger than ever.
In one week's time, we will fight.
And we will win."
Ember then glanced at the soldiers one last time and,
"You are all dismissed,"
She ordered.
