chapters.title: Chapter 1836 Tandris and its Three Races.
paragraphs: 350 flying ships hovered like titanic shadows in the vast Universe.
These ships were the Gift Velcria had received from its Faction. Their Treasure, an Artifact that allowed the people of Velcria to travel in the vast Outer Space.

These ships not only had barriers that were capable of protecting it and the people inside it from the poisonous Universal Energy for as long as these barriers can be reinforced with energy, but they were also capable of carrying around 3,000 beings without any issues, making it one of the greatest inventions that made mass travel possible.

The fleet of 350 ships formed a disciplined formation, resembling an unbreakable wall. The lead ship, Aurora's Heart, was the largest and most radiant, its hull gleaming with golden runes. Inside the Ship, Ember, together with her Sisters and the Velcria Leaders, stood tall, looking at Tandris that loomed below them.

Tandris was a dark world pulsating with ominous energy. Its surface was a stark contrast to Velcria's vibrant beauty. It had a harsh, hot environment. Rugged terrain cloaked in perpetual shadows, uneven volcanic eruptions all over the place, and its atmosphere swirled with crimson and black storms.
"That doesn't look like a place one would want to live in."
Allura commented as she observed the dark world from above.
"Tandris was never an inhabitable place, especially for a race like ours."
Liora replied. Out of all the people, she was the most uncomfortable at the thought of going to this cursed world.

The world's dark energy was in complete contrast with hers. This was also one of the reasons Velcria hadn't been able to take over and defeat the enemy world. One of their three forces felt the same discomfort that Liora felt, making it difficult for them to perform.

And it weren't just the Seraphytes who had a problem with this environment; Sylvanix, a race close to nature, felt the same. Their aversion and disgust weren't as strong as the Seraphytes', but it was still there.
And seeing how the Sylvanix leader Elaris was nodding her head at Liora's words, the girls could see that.
"Well, the races living there aren't particularly pleasing to the eyes either."
Aisha commented. In her hands were the papers that carried information about the three races of Tandris.
Yes, the women had done their research before accepting the mission. However,
Ember believed that it was wise to ask Velcria Leaders to give them every piece of information they had about the enemies.
After all, the Mercenary Hall couldn't possibly know more about Tandris and its people than their long-standing enemies, could they?
"Anyways, just so we are all on the same page,
You all have read about the enemies we will be facing, correct?"

Ember questioned as she stared at her sisters. Her gaze lingering a little longer on Allura, Aisha, Edda, and Skyla. The four women seemed offended, especially Edda, so she stepped forward, placing a paper on the table.

On the paper, there was a picture of a being: a pale humanoid with a shadowy aura around him, his hollow eyes glowing red like smoldering embers. His skin seemed to have the ability to absorb light, giving him a spectral, ghost-like presence.
Picture
"Dreadborn."
Edda started.
"Appearance, Ugly.
Important Abilities: Devour, Shadow Walk, and Aura of Dread.
The first one allows them to devour opponents' Life Force or Energy to Heal themselves or amplify their powers.
The second allows them to travel through shadows.
And the last one allows them to spread fear and whatever.
What we need to worry about is just Devour, so don't let these things get close to you.
The Aura of Dread doesn't matter; Skyla and Ember's Law will protect us.
As for Shadow Walk, well, if they try to move in your shadow, let them.
I wanna see what happens."
Edda chuckled. The rest of the women shook their heads, but they all had smiles on their faces. Just imagining the scene made them laugh out loud.
The three Velcria Leaders frowned, unable to understand what these women were
laughing about.
Edda, however, completely ignored them and continued.
"Dreadborns usually act as spics, assassins, and strategists. They excel in
psychological warfare and would 100% try to disrupt our formations before the battle
even begins.
Not that it would matter."
Edda shrugged as she stared at Ember, the woman had complete confidence in her General.
"Anyways, your turn."
Edda glanced at Allura, and the Succubus stepped forward, putting another picture on the table.
This time, it was a towering being with his skin resembling molten lava. His horns curved sharply backward, and his eyes shimmered with fiery intensity.
Picture
"Inferniks."
She started.
"Appearance, Ugly.
Important abilities: Hellfire Manipulation, Infernal Resilience, Cataclysmic Strike.

Meh, just some fancy names for the ability to control fire, a durable body that cannot be attacked with fire-based attacks since that would only strengthen them, and releasing shockwaves of fire that could be somewhat useful when dealing with
multiple enemies.
They are the 'frontline warriors and siege specialists, have higher raw power than
most, so our soldiers need to be somewhat careful."
Allura shrugged, then glanced at Aisha, who sighed and stepped forward.
The picture she placed on the table was of the third race of Tandris.
An ethereal, wraith-like being made of semi-translucent, shadowy mist. Ilis faintly glowing eyes hovered within an undefined face.
Picture
"Nightveil,
Ugly.
Abilities: Void Rift, Phantom Form, Mind Shroud.
Well, they can disrupt Mana Flow, making it difficult for us to use our abilities. Phantom Form makes them somewhat immune to physical attacks, and Mind Shroud
is just a fancy name for illusion and mind control.
They can turn our soldiers against each other, but honestly, it won't matter if they are under Ember's Law, so it is not a big deal.
They are somewhat similar to the Dreadborns, they confuse enemies and roam around
in the battlefield in a ghost-like manner to cause chaos.
We have read everything, okay?
Are we done here?"
Aisha questioned with a tired sigh.
"You didn't let me speak."𝓯𝓻𝒆𝙚𝒘𝓮𝙗𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝒍.𝙘𝓸𝙢
Skyla pouted.
"You summarise their unified roles in the War!"
Ember ordered, and with a big smile on her face, Skyla nodded.
"The Dreadborns weaken and scatter enemy forces with fear and assassination.

The Inferniks charge the front lines, breaking defenses with overwhelming power. The Nightveil dominate the battlefield with disorienting magic and illusions. And of course, Tandris's Will would make them stronger while our soldiers will be at a
slight disadvantage."
Skyla summarised everything clearly, and Ember nodded, satisfied.
"Alright, that will be enough."
The General then stared at Liora, the Seraphyte Leader, who nodded.
Ember then pressed the button, her golden armor gleaming under the faint light of the
ship's runes. Her image appeared on the projection screens across all 350 ships, and,
"Soldiers of Velcria."
She called out.

Ember believed that it was wise to ask Velcria Leaders to give them every piece of information they had about the enemies.
After all, the Mercenary Hall couldn't possibly know more about Tandris and its people than their long-standing enemies, could they?
"Anyways, just so we are all on the same page,
You all have read about the enemies we will be facing, correct?"
Ember questioned as she stared at her sisters.
Her gaze lingering a little longer on Allura, Aisha, Edda, and Skyla.
The four women seemed offended, especially Edda, so she stepped forward, placing a paper on the table.
On the paper, there was a picture of a being: a pale humanoid with a shadowy aura around him, his hollow eyes glowing red like smoldering embers.
His skin seemed to have the ability to absorb light, giving him a spectral, ghost-like presence.
Picture
"Dreadborn."
Edda started.
"Appearance, Ugly.
Important Abilities: Devour, Shadow Walk, and Aura of Dread.
The first one allows them to devour opponents' Life Force or Energy to Heal themselves or amplify their powers.
The second allows them to travel through shadows.
And the last one allows them to spread fear and whatever.
What we need to worry about is just Devour, so don't let these things get close to you.
The Aura of Dread doesn't matter; Skyla and Ember's Law will protect us.
As for Shadow Walk, well, if they try to move in your shadow, let them.
I wanna see what happens."
Edda chuckled.
The rest of the women shook their heads, but they all had smiles on their faces.
Just imagining the scene made them laugh out loud.
The three Velcria Leaders frowned, unable to understand what these women were
laughing about.
Edda, however, completely ignored them and continued.
"Dreadborns usually act as spics, assassins, and strategists.
They excel in
psychological warfare and would 100% try to disrupt our formations before the battle
even begins.
Not that it would matter."
Edda shrugged as she stared at Ember, the woman had complete confidence in her General.
"Anyways, your turn."
Edda glanced at Allura, and the Succubus stepped forward, putting another picture on the table.
This time, it was a towering being with his skin resembling molten lava.
His horns curved sharply backward, and his eyes shimmered with fiery intensity.
Picture
"Inferniks."
She started.
"Appearance, Ugly.
Important abilities: Hellfire Manipulation, Infernal Resilience, Cataclysmic Strike.

Meh, just some fancy names for the ability to control fire, a durable body that cannot be attacked with fire-based attacks since that would only strengthen them, and releasing shockwaves of fire that could be somewhat useful when dealing with
multiple enemies.
They are the 'frontline warriors and siege specialists, have higher raw power than
most, so our soldiers need to be somewhat careful."
Allura shrugged, then glanced at Aisha, who sighed and stepped forward.
The picture she placed on the table was of the third race of Tandris.
An ethereal, wraith-like being made of semi-translucent, shadowy mist.
Ilis faintly glowing eyes hovered within an undefined face.
Picture
"Nightveil,
Ugly.
Abilities: Void Rift, Phantom Form, Mind Shroud.
Well, they can disrupt Mana Flow, making it difficult for us to use our abilities.
Phantom Form makes them somewhat immune to physical attacks, and Mind Shroud
is just a fancy name for illusion and mind control.
They can turn our soldiers against each other, but honestly, it won't matter if they are under Ember's Law, so it is not a big deal.
They are somewhat similar to the Dreadborns, they confuse enemies and roam around
in the battlefield in a ghost-like manner to cause chaos.
We have read everything, okay?
Are we done here?"
Aisha questioned with a tired sigh.
"You didn't let me speak."𝓯𝓻𝒆𝙚𝒘𝓮𝙗𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝒍.𝙘𝓸𝙢
Skyla pouted.
"You summarise their unified roles in the War!"
Ember ordered, and with a big smile on her face, Skyla nodded.
"The Dreadborns weaken and scatter enemy forces with fear and assassination.
The Inferniks charge the front lines, breaking defenses with overwhelming power.
The Nightveil dominate the battlefield with disorienting magic and illusions.
And of course, Tandris's Will would make them stronger while our soldiers will be at a
slight disadvantage."
Skyla summarised everything clearly, and Ember nodded, satisfied.
"Alright, that will be enough."
The General then stared at Liora, the Seraphyte Leader, who nodded.
Ember then pressed the button, her golden armor gleaming under the faint light of the
ship's runes.
Her image appeared on the projection screens across all 350 ships, and,
"Soldiers of Velcria."
She called out.

chapters.title: Chapter 1837: FOR VELCRIA!!!
paragraphs: "Soldiers of Velcria."
She called out.

The Soldiers, who heard her voice, instantly turned towards the projection screen and, seeing their General, her party, and their Leaders standing together, a slight sense of relief and calm washed over them.
This was an all-out War; even in the long history of Velcria, there had only been five such Wars, and in all those Wars, the losses Velcria faced were immense.
Many soldiers had died, and it was only natural for the Velcrian soldiers to feel slightly nervous as their ships hovered above Tandris.

However, the instant they heard Ember’s voice, the Soldiers, especially the Soldiers who were part of Ember’s Force during the demonstration, stood up, their eyes glimmering with unmatched excitement and zeal.
It was the Goddess of War!
Yes, this was the name these Soldiers had given to Ember.
Unlike other soldiers, they weren’t scared or nervous. Their faith in Ember was Absolute; it was almost absurd. A Cult-like Faith.

And these soldiers couldn’t be blamed either. They had seen and felt the Goddess’s power on themselves, and they highly doubted that a world like Tandris could stand in front of their Goddess’s might.

Actually, it wasn’t just Ember’s soldiers who thought this way. The rest of the soldiers, who had continuously heard how remarkable the ’Goddess’ was, were also hoping for the Goddess to use her magic and save their lives.
They were all counting on her, and hearing her voice and knowing that she was with them even now reassured them.
"I know what you’re thinking.
I know what you’re feeling.
There are whispers around the fleets, talks of losses, of sacrifices, of what could go wrong.
It’s natural.
War isn’t kind.
And the fear of the unknown can gnaw at even the strongest of hearts.
But let me make one thing clear right now.
This War was ours to win from the beginning.
It was never about which side is stronger; that may have been the case before, but now,
You have me."
Ember declared.
The soldiers stared at her and then at each other, different emotions reflecting in their eyes.
"And that changes everything.
I have shown it before, and now I will show it again on a larger scale.
I only have to say one thing, the thing I have been saying since the very start,
As long as you follow my orders to the letter, nothing will stand in your way.
Nothing."
Ember spoke, her eyes moving as if she could see every single one of the soldiers present in all 350 fleets.
The soldiers couldn’t take their eyes away from the Goddess of War either; it was as if their minds were struck, taken over by the woman in front of them.
"This isn’t a battle of survival; it’s a battle of annihilation.
And I’m not talking about some long, drawn-out, bloody war that drags on until we’re half-dead, waiting for a win.
No. I’m talking about an overwhelming victory
A victory so decisive that when the dust settles, our enemies will look around and wonder how they ever thought they stood a chance."
Ember declared confidently, her eyes glimmering with a merciless look. Then, she stared at her soldiers again and, with a reassuring tone, she continued,
"I’ve seen the battlefield,
I’ve studied our enemies,
Their weaknesses? I already know them all, and I’ll exploit every single one of them.
But here’s the thing, this will only work if you trust me.
You follow my commands, you stay synchronized with me, and you give everything you’ve got.
When I say go, you go.
When I say hold, you hold.
When I say strike, you strike,
And you strike with everything you’ve got.
There’s no room for hesitation. You will not second-guess me. That’s how we win.
We move as one, and united, we will be unstoppable.
I don’t care what they throw at us. I don’t care how many they are or what they have. As long as you follow my orders, we will decimate them.
So, I’ll say it again.
We are going to win this, and we are going to win with no casualties.
Victory is ours.
Let’s take it."
Ember spoke in a firm tone. Then, she raised her sword and,
"For Velcria."
And the instant she said these words, as if enlightenment had struck the soldiers, they all shouted in unison.
"FOR VELCRIA!!!"
"FOR VELCRIA!!!"
"FOR VELCRIA!!!"
The 350 fleets rumbled, shaken by the cries of a million soldiers.
Then, something that surprised even Ember happened,
BOOM BOOM BOOM BOOM
On all the fleets spread across the space, the soldiers’ Aura burst out, not one, two, hundred, or thousand…
All One Million Soldiers had their Auras and their strength boosted by Ember’s Law.
Yes, all the soldiers present here had accepted her as their true General.
"FOR VELCRIA!!!"
"FOR VELCRIA!!!"
"FOR VELCRIA!!!"
The Soldiers continued to shout, their chants echoing through the space. It was as if the very Universal Energy was carrying their sound.
"…are they trying to alert the enemy?"
Kaelgran couldn’t help but frown in confusion.
"Leave it be,
The enemy should already know."
Ember shrugged, not giving it too much thought.
"What…?"
Kaelgran, however, couldn’t believe her words.
"What? You don’t think every single person in Velcria is loyal to it, do you?"
Ember questioned with a smile, and Kaelgran turned silent.
"Tandris must have planted a few spies; it is not a surprise.
The good thing is that there are only about a thousand spies amongst our soldiers."
"What did you say? There are spies in our army?"
"Is it that surprising?"
"No, but… are you saying you know who they are?"
Liora questioned as she stared at Ember with a careful look on her face.
"Well, there are about a thousand soldiers who are not connected with me yet. Either they are extremely paranoid, or…"
"They are spies…"
Liora completed Ember’s sentence, a cold glint appearing in her usual gentle eyes.
"Well, we will find out soon enough. There is no need to worry about it."
Ember shrugged.
Then, she pointed at the world below them and,
"Attack."
She commanded, and 350 ships entered Tandris’s environment like vultures prepared to decimate their enemies.

chapters.title: Chapter 1838: War 1
paragraphs: Whoosh Whoosh Whoosh
Strong wind currents flew as if there was a world-ending storm nearby.
Thunder Thunder Thunder
The clouds roared in anger, as if trying to alert every single being in the world.
Rumble Rumble Rumble
The ground shook, trembling non-stop; it was as if the world itself was reacting.
And it was.
Tandris was angered as 350 Velcrian ships descended from outer space, breaching its atmosphere. The ships’ glowing hulls cut through the swirling crimson and black storms of Tandris’ atmosphere.
It was a spectacle of precision and power, a wall of golden light shimmering against the oppressive darkness of the planet below.
"FOR VELCRIA!!!"
"FOR VELCRIA!!!"
"FOR VELCRIA!!!"
The Velcrian ships and the soldiers’ bellow broke through the thick, toxic clouds of Tandris, and soon the capital, Draventhis, revealed itself in all its foreboding glory.
The city was a fortress.

Tall, jagged towers of obsidian reached for the skies, pulsating with a faint, sickly red glow. Rivers of molten lava crisscrossed its surface, flowing into massive forges and pits that powered the city.
Bzzzz
The skies above Draventhis were illuminated by a shield dome, a shimmering barrier that buzzed with ethereal runes of crimson and black.
This was the Shield of Aegis, Tandris’ strongest defense, an artifact gifted by their faction to withstand even the mightiest of assaults.
Inside Velcria’s main fleet, the Aurora’s Heart, Ember stood at the helm, observing the capital city beneath her.
"Draventhis is prepared, just like you said."
Liora muttered, her wings twitching slightly as she observed the shield.
She, however, didn’t seem surprised. Unlike Kaelgran, she knew there was never an ’element of surprise’ in this war.
"That shield…
It will be hard to break."
Elaris muttered as she narrowed her eyes, staring at the shield in front of her.
"It doesn’t have to be easy. It just has to be done."
Ember spoke with a cold look on her face.
Once again, she pressed the button that allowed her to contact all the ships under her command.
"All ships, prepare for assault.
Focus fire on the shield.
We break it now."
The woman commanded.
Bzzzz
A symphony of energy roared to life as the Velcrian ships shimmered brightly.
It was the ships’ attack feature, a mixture of energy cannons, concentrated beam weapons, and kinetic projectiles activated in unison.𝒻𝘳𝘦𝘦𝘸ℯ𝒷𝘯𝘰𝑣ℯ𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝘮
Whoosh
BOOOOOOOOOM
Blinding streams of golden light lanced out from the fleet, crashing into the shield with deafening force. The impact reverberated through the air, shaking the ground beneath Draventhis.
Yes, this was the plan. They would use artifacts given by the faction to counter the artifacts given by the faction.
Bzzzzzzz
The Shield of Aegis flickered violently, runes drawn on it glowing brighter than ever.
"ATTACK THE ENEMY!!"
BOOM BOOM BOOM
From within Draventhis, the Tandris forces retaliated.
Infernik siege cannons fired blazing infernos into the sky, while Dreadborn shadow-strikes attempted to disrupt the ships’ formations.
"Hold formation!"
Ember commanded, her voice unwavering amidst the chaos.
"Do not falter!
Increase energy output!"
Her words echoed all over the 350 fleets.

The Velcria leaders remained silent. Just like Ember, they knew breaking the shield was their highest priority. Yes, it did put them at a disadvantage since using the ships’ cannons drained the soldiers’ energy, while the Tandris forces, who were prepared for the siege, had activated the shield using energy stones, saving their soldiers’ energy.
However, they had no other option.

For several tense minutes, the shield held firm. Tandris soldiers continued to attack Velcria’s ships. Most of their attacks, however, were blocked by the ships’ barriers. Both sides knew that this couldn’t go on.

Velcria soldiers would fall even before the war began since the ships’ cannons and barriers were draining their energy. Even if they had potions to regenerate their energy, the potions weren’t endless.
Soon, however, something changed.
Crack Crack Crack
Cracks began to form on the Shield of Aegis, thin spiderwebs of energy spreading across its surface.
The moment she noticed that, Ember turned towards the three Primordials and,
"Now!"
She nodded.
The Velcria leaders nodded and injected their energy into the ships. The ships unleashed a final barrage, and,
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM
A blinding surge of energy shattered the shield with an ear-piercing explosion.
"Shield’s down!"
Skyla announced with a wide grin on her face as she turned towards her sister.
Ember wasted no time either.
"Velcrian warriors, this is your moment.
Begin the invasion!"
"FOR VELCRIA!!!"
"FOR VELCRIA!!!"
"FOR VELCRIA!!!"
The ships’ doors opened, and one million soldiers, clad in the gleaming armor of Velcria, jumped from the ships in synchronized precision.
It was like a meteor shower.
Golden streaks of light rained down upon the dark city of Draventhis.
"CRUSH THEM!!!"
"DESTROY THE ENEMIES!"
The Tandris forces, waiting within the city, roared in response.
The Inferniks surged forward, their molten bodies glowing like small suns as they clashed with Velcrian Stoneborns.
The Dreadborn emerged from the shadows, attempting to ambush descending soldiers, only to be met by Seraphytes, who blocked their attacks and protected their allies.
BOOM BOOM BOOM
The clashes became more and more chaotic.
The Tandris forces continued to attack the descending Velcrian forces, while the Velcrian forces defended themselves, trying to invade now that the barrier had shattered.
As the chaos spread all over the place, Ember herself leaped from the Aurora’s Heart, followed by her sisters.
The three Velcrian leaders still didn’t move.
They were waiting for the enemy leaders to make a move.
In wars, the victory and defeat of the army were decided by the victory and defeat of the world leaders, so most of the time, the Primordials do not waste their energy fighting Sovereigns.
They saved their energy for the last, waiting for a moment the enemy made a mistake that they could take advantage of.
Till then, it was a battle between the two armies.
’Heh, this is fun~’
Aisha laughed as she flew in the air, protecting the soldiers from the enemy attack.
’This is your first war, isn’t it?’
Allura questioned.
’The one where I have an army on my side? Yeah.
The others mostly had Nux going crazy and doing all that ridiculously absurd stuff.’
’Ouch, why am I being attacked here?’
Nux complained.
’Shut the hell up, let me enjoy.’
Aisha laughed as she finally landed on the ground with the soldiers.
Within a few minutes, the two forces were against each other, this time, on the grounds of Tandris.

They saved their energy for the last, waiting for a moment the enemy made a mistake that they could take advantage of.
Till then, it was a battle between the two armies.
’Heh, this is fun~’
Aisha laughed as she flew in the air, protecting the soldiers from the enemy attack.
’This is your first war, isn’t it?’
Allura questioned.
’The one where I have an army on my side?
Yeah.
The others mostly had Nux going crazy and doing all that ridiculously absurd stuff.’
’Ouch, why am I being attacked here?’
Nux complained.
’Shut the hell up, let me enjoy.’
Aisha laughed as she finally landed on the ground with the soldiers.
Within a few minutes, the two forces were against each other, this time, on the grounds of Tandris.

chapters.title: Chapter 1839: War 2
paragraphs: The two sides rushed at each other without wasting time. The high-ranking commanders on both sides knew from a very long time that both sides were equally strong.
This was the reason Tandris soldiers were confident. With Tandris’s will on their side, how could they possibly lose?
The Velcrains were rushing to their deaths.
Or at least… that’s what they thought…
Today, however, things were different.
’Seraphytes Unit Three, take to the skies. Target the Inferniks on the southern flank.’
The Seraphytes soldiers heard Ember’s calm voice in their heads, and as if someone had taken control of their bodies, they moved.𝓯𝓻𝓮𝙚𝙬𝓮𝙗𝒏𝙤𝒗𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝒐𝓶
Whoosh Whoosh Whoosh
Their radiant wings illuminated the darkened battlefield. Bolts of golden light rained down on the hulking Inferniks, cutting through their molten armor with precision.
A group of Seraphytes formed a protective dome of shimmering light around the Stoneborn warriors holding the line below, deflecting the devastating Hellfire attacks.
’Seraphyte Unit Four, support the left flank with barriers.’
Ember ordered, and another cluster of Seraphytes broke formation, their combined light forming an impenetrable wall that stopped the advance of Tandris forces attempting to encircle Velcria’s troops.
’Stoneborns Unit Two, advance five paces and create fissures beneath the Dreadborn.’
Rumble Rumble Rumble
At her words, the earth trembled as the Stoneborn stomped forward in unison, their fists pounding the ground.
Crack Crack Crack
Massive cracks split the battlefield, swallowing Tandris soldiers whole. Those who weren’t caught in the fissures found themselves stumbling, unable to maintain their balance.
’Form a wedge and push through their center.’
’Sylvanix Unit Three, cover their flanks.’
The Stoneborn Unit reformed with a discipline uncharacteristic of their usually individualistic nature, their massive bodies bulldozing through Tandris ranks.
BOOM BOOM BOOM
Their stone gauntlets crushed Inferniks with terrifying ease, while their rocky skin shrugged off Hellfire blasts and void rifts alike.
’Sylvanix Unit One, spread out. I need vines choking their cavalry.’

The Sylvanix moved with unparalleled agility. Their vines erupted from the ground, tangling and toppling Tandris’s mounted forces. Thorn barrages struck the enemy soldiers with fearsome precision, disarming them before they could regroup.
’Deploy healing spores to the Stoneborn front lines. They must hold until the Seraphytes neutralize the Inferniks.’
Ember’s commands were heard again, and a golden mist spread across the battlefield as Sylvanix Unit released their rejuvenating spores, mending wounds and revitalizing the Stoneborns ahead.
"What in the hell is happening!?"
One of the Tandris commanders standing on an elevated platform screamed in rage, and it wasn’t just him with these questions. The rest of the commanders were the same.
"The Inferniks should have broken their lines by now! How are they the ones being pushed back!? Why haven’t they taken down the enemy Seraphytes yet!?"

"What is wrong with the enemy soldiers!? Why are they faster and stronger than I remember!? Does any of you remember a normal Stoneborn Unit being strong enough to create fissures all over the ground!? How are they doing that!?"
"The Sylvanix aren’t normal either. They have not only captured the Inferniks and the Dreadborn using their vines, but they are also healing the Stoneborns we had barely managed to injure!"
"My Unit’s Aura of Dread isn’t working either!"

A Dreadborn commander shared a problem. He had been trying to get into the heads of the enemy soldiers to try and get some advantage, but no matter what he did, nothing worked. It was as if his powers were being blocked by some kind of barrier he couldn’t see.
"My Unit’s Mind Shroud isn’t working either!"
A Nightveil commander was facing the same problem.
"Something is wrong with the enemies!"
The commanders reached the same conclusion.

"These are not the enemies we had faced in all the skirmishes before. These soldiers are too strong and well-coordinated. Even a random unit from their army is pushing our elite force like children playing with sticks!

We are unable to catch them by surprise. Even if we somehow manage to hurt them, another unit arrives to heal them the next instant. If we try to surround them, our formation breaks in the middle, and our soldiers are the ones who end up getting surrounded!
This is not Velcria!
It is almost as if we are facing completely different beings!"

These commanders weren’t new. They had thousands of years of experience. These beings had been facing enemies from Velcria even before the war between the two factions started, and because of that, they could tell.
Something was wrong.
Something was extremely wrong.
The rate at which their soldiers were being crushed was simply too high. The enemy was too overwhelmingly powerful.
They were supposed to be the winning side here. How are they being pushed back to this extent!? If this goes on, it wouldn’t take the enemies more than a few hours to completely annihilate them!
"It must be that woman!"
Suddenly, the Nightveil commander shouted as he pointed at Ember.
"The Goddess of War! She must be the Goddess of War the spies reported about!"
"Haah!? Does that make any sense!?"
Another commander shouted.
"Is whatever’s happening making any sense to you!?"
The Nightveil commander shot back.
"We need to take her down."
The Nightveil commander ordered, his hollow dark eyes narrowed as he stared at other commanders.
The rest of the five commanders nodded.
"We need to come up with a plan.
A plan to get rid of that woman as soon as possible.
We need to assassinate her."
The commanders had decided.
As she hovered in the air, Ember saw everything. Every movement, every weakness, every opportunity. Her mind worked faster than anyone else’s, processing the chaos with cold, calculated precision.
This was her forte. This was her ground.
This was where General Ember shined the brightest.
’Tandris is reinforcing their northern flank.’
She noted, her golden eyes shining as she spotted a cluster of Nightveil drifting ominously toward the vulnerable area.
’Seraphytes Unit Two, focus fire on the Nightveil in the north.’
She commanded, and golden beams of light sliced through the shadows, disrupting the Nightveil’s phantom forms. The spectral beings recoiled, their void rifts collapsing before they could even form.

’Stoneborn Unit Three, shift to protect the northern flank. Sylvanix Unit Five, cover their retreat, and Unit Two, attack the Dreadborns behind you with poison clouds while Stoneborn Unit One attacks them.’
The Units she commanded moved at a surprising speed.

With a million soldiers all under the effect of the Law of Boundless Unity, the Velcria army was strengthened to an absurd degree. This, combined with Ember’s eyes that watched over the entire battlefield and her ability to command her soldiers with such precision,
Tandris Army was in shambles.
A complete one-sided war. No, this was no war.
It was a massacre.
A massacre of Tandris’s soldiers.
’Ember.’
Suddenly, Rune called out.
Ember didn’t reply. The cat woman, however, knew that her sister was listening, so she continued.
’Six of their commanders, Peak Divines.’
The cat woman warned.
Ember, however, just chuckled and,
’Let them come.
It is a good opportunity to deal with six high-ranking soldiers at the same time.’
Yes, the Velcria General was actually waiting for the enemy commanders to come and try to assassinate her.

chapters.title: Chapter 1840: The Blood Sovereign
paragraphs: ’Ember.
Six of their commanders, Peak Divines.’
The Cat woman warned.
Ember, however, just chuckled and nodded at her sister.
Rune nodded back and continued to keep her eye on the commanders who were going after Ember while she followed them, just in case something went wrong.
These commanders were carrying a prism-shaped artifact that they called Chains of Soul.

While Rune wasn’t worried about their strength, both these worlds were supported by their Factions, Factions that originated from High-Level Worlds, because of that, they possessed artifacts she and her sisters had never seen or heard about before.

Even Velcria possessed a few artifacts whose functions surprised them, and since these artifacts were created by Higher-Level Worlds, some were made for beings on Primordial or even Transcendent Levels. It was extremely difficult, if not outright impossible, to counter them. Discover stories with Freewebnovel
Of course, the Factions usually didn’t give such strong artifacts to Low-Level Worlds, but Rune was still worried.
Rune wanted to know what the enemy was planning; however, knowing that she couldn’t do that herself, she decided to call her ally.
An ally that even she, one of the strongest Sovereigns amongst her sisters, was currently intimidated by.
’Their abilities are broken.’
Rune thought inwardly as she glanced in the direction of her sister.
Yes, it was a war. It was Ember’s playing field. The place where she shined the brightest.
But…
Ember wasn’t the only being who thrived in wars or in group battles.
There was someone else.
Melia Leander.

At first, it wasn’t a big deal. Melia, just like her sisters, was attacking enemy Sovereigns and was actually at quite a disadvantage. If it weren’t for Ember’s Law strengthening her, she might have even lost, but…
The Vampire won.
And it didn’t end there.
After she won, her blood moved inside the enemy she had killed, turning him into her puppet.
Now, Melia was as strong as two Sovereigns. She and her puppet then attacked another Sovereign. This time, the battle was much simpler and quicker.
Now, Melia had two undead Sovereigns under her control.
Then the number increased to three, four, six, ten…
Of course, all this time, she didn’t ignore the Protector-level soldiers either. There were about 100 of them under her control, and the number continued to increase even further.

As more time passed, the amount of blood all around the battlefield continued to rise as the soldiers killed each other without mercy. The cruelty of a battlefield was visible for all to see, and in this cruelty, amongst all this blood,
The Blood Sovereign got stronger.
Right now, the Vampire was taking on 5000 soldiers, an entire Unit of the Tandris Army, on her own. One had to know, more than 1000 of these soldiers were Sovereigns, just like her.

The woman had created her domain of Blood, a domain where blood flowed, not just on the ground, but hovered in the air as well. The blood was under the Vampire’s complete control, doing everything she wanted it to.
With her at the center, this woman could control all the blood 10 km away from her, effectively covering more than 300 square kilometers of area. And this area that was under her control,
It was hell for her enemies.
Blood flowed in the air, ready to pierce through their bodies any time the Blood Sovereign desired, making it absurdly difficult to close the distance between them and the one controlling the blood.
It was a nightmare.
A nightmare the Tandris soldiers couldn’t wake up from.
"What is this!? What is this monster!? Are we sure she is only a Sovereign!?"
The Unit Commander couldn’t believe his eyes.

His soldiers were being killed at a rate he never even thought was possible. Knowing that he could not let this continue for long because the longer he waited, the more soldiers he would lose, strengthening the enemy’s ’undead army’ instead, the Commander decided to move.
Four hundred of his best men, all Sovereigns, were selected to be an Elite Battalion. This Battalion was to move and finish the enemy once and for all.
It was a simple plan. While the rest of his soldiers took on the blood puppets under this woman’s control, his Elite Battalion would take on this woman.
How could a single Sovereign, no matter how strong, take on 400 Sovereigns all on her own?
Heck, the commander even ordered the injured soldiers to act as living shields, protecting the Sovereigns as they moved toward Melia.
It had essentially turned into a 1 vs. 400.
And soon, Melia was overwhelmed by her enemies.
As strong as she was, she was quickly surrounded until finally, one of the Sovereigns was able to slice her arm.
"Yes!"
The moment he saw that, the commander’s eyes brightened up.
"Don’t let her run away, end it here!
Let her pay the price for killing our comrades!
Kill her!"
He commanded, his excited voice resounding throughout the battlefield, but then,
Something happened.
Whoosh Whoosh Whoosh
The blood flowing in the air entered Melia’s body. Her severed arm that had fallen on the ground turned into a pile of blood, and an entirely new arm regrew in its stead.
What’s worse?

All of this happened in milliseconds. It was so fast that one couldn’t even tell that her arm had been sliced off. And as if knowing that this would happen, Melia, who had never stopped her attacks, continued moving and killed the Sovereign who had attacked her, along with a few others.
And this didn’t just happen once. Every time the enemy Sovereigns were able to land a successful hit and injure her to some extent, the woman regenerated back to full health that very instant.
It didn’t matter if they cut off her arms, legs, or even her head; the blood flowing in the air moved into her body and regenerated her. Even cutting her into half or piercing her heart didn’t work.
As long as there was enough blood, she was an immortal.
An Absolute.
And on the battlefield…
The only thing that was in abundance was this blood.
Let alone 400, she could face any number of Sovereigns since she could never die in the first place.
"W-What in the hell is she…?"
The enemy commander couldn’t believe it.
With Ember’s Law that had strengthened her, combined with her own ability that pretty much turned her into an immortal with rivers of blood flowing around her,
Melia faced 400 Sovereigns on her own.

The blood around her obeyed her every command, bounding, blinding, and attacking the enemy. It even formed shields that protected her from enemy attacks, and every time she was hurt, the blood entered her body and healed her back to full health.
Whatever the enemies did, it was all useless.
The so-called ’Elite Battalion’ looked like a bunch of moths rushing towards the flames, dying in the process.
And what’s worse?
All these Sovereigns were turning into Melia’s puppets, making her even stronger than before.
The commander, who realized that, widened his eyes in horror.
’This works even on Sovereigns!?’
He, however, didn’t have too much time to think.
"All units—advance!
Don’t stop! We take her down now, or we all die here!
MOVE! MOVE!
Leave the puppets behind!"
He ordered.
If 400 Sovereigns were not enough, he would attack with more than 1,000 Sovereigns. He would use the strength of his entire Unit to take down this monster!
As for the puppets his soldiers were facing? It didn’t matter. They needed to leave them behind. The puppets would fall once the master fell.
Yes, this method would increase the number of casualties, but they didn’t have another answer.
They needed to kill this monster as soon as possible.
But…
It was all useless.
400 or 1,000, to the current Melia surrounded with so much blood, it didn’t matter.
She was undefeatable.
The Commander and his Unit were absolutely helpless.

Their fate was decided the instant Melia had appeared in front of them, and it was to die at her hands and turn into her puppets, aiding her as she grew her ’army’ and took down more enemy Units, growing her influence in the War.
All on her own.
This was Melia Leander,
The Blood Sovereign.
A being that even Ember had stopped commanding and decided to let her do whatever she wanted.

A being that started from a single Sovereign, now took down an entire Unit, and would now be targeting another Unit, defeating it with much more ease until finally, she grew her ’army’ to the point it was able to take on more than one enemy Unit at the same time.
Yes, the longer this War continued, the stronger this monster’s presence would become.
A presence that even the enemy Primordials wouldn’t be able to ignore.
Rune, who was watching Melia, was lost for a second.
Soon, however, she came out of her reverie and called her sister.
’Ummm… Melia, a little help here would be appreciated…’

The moment she said those words, she suddenly noticed Melia’s entire body turning into a puddle of blood while her Sovereign Level blood puppets, whose numbers were now higher than enemy Sovereigns by a large margin, continued to attack.
Rune frowned, not knowing what happened. Then suddenly,
"What is it?"
She heard a voice that made her jump in fright as she then turned around, only to see Melia staring at her.
"How- no, when did you come here—"
"I have placed blood marks all over the battlefield since I came here.
I can teleport anywhere I want to."
Melia revealed, and Rune just stared at this monster, not knowing what to say.
For the first time, the cat woman actually wondered if her Law was strong enough to be amongst this bunch of monsters.

Let alone 400, she could face any number of Sovereigns since she could never die in the first place.
"W-What in the hell is she…?"
The enemy commander couldn’t believe it.
With Ember’s Law that had strengthened her, combined with her own ability that pretty much turned her into an immortal with rivers of blood flowing around her,
Melia faced 400 Sovereigns on her own.
The blood around her obeyed her every command, bounding, blinding, and attacking the enemy.
It even formed shields that protected her from enemy attacks, and every time she was hurt, the blood entered her body and healed her back to full health.
Whatever the enemies did, it was all useless.
The so-called ’Elite Battalion’ looked like a bunch of moths rushing towards the flames, dying in the process.
And what’s worse?
All these Sovereigns were turning into Melia’s puppets, making her even stronger than before.
The commander, who realized that, widened his eyes in horror.
’This works even on Sovereigns!?’
He, however, didn’t have too much time to think.
"All units—advance!
Don’t stop!
We take her down now, or we all die here!
MOVE!
MOVE!
Leave the puppets behind!"
He ordered.
If 400 Sovereigns were not enough, he would attack with more than 1,000 Sovereigns.
He would use the strength of his entire Unit to take down this monster!
As for the puppets his soldiers were facing?
It didn’t matter.
They needed to leave them behind.
The puppets would fall once the master fell.
Yes, this method would increase the number of casualties, but they didn’t have another answer.
They needed to kill this monster as soon as possible.
But…
It was all useless.
400 or 1,000, to the current Melia surrounded with so much blood, it didn’t matter.
She was undefeatable.
The Commander and his Unit were absolutely helpless.

Their fate was decided the instant Melia had appeared in front of them, and it was to die at her hands and turn into her puppets, aiding her as she grew her ’army’ and took down more enemy Units, growing her influence in the War.
All on her own.
This was Melia Leander,
The Blood Sovereign.
A being that even Ember had stopped commanding and decided to let her do whatever she wanted.

A being that started from a single Sovereign, now took down an entire Unit, and would now be targeting another Unit, defeating it with much more ease until finally, she grew her ’army’ to the point it was able to take on more than one enemy Unit at the same time.
Yes, the longer this War continued, the stronger this monster’s presence would become.
A presence that even the enemy Primordials wouldn’t be able to ignore.
Rune, who was watching Melia, was lost for a second.
Soon, however, she came out of her reverie and called her sister.
’Ummm…
Melia, a little help here would be appreciated…’

The moment she said those words, she suddenly noticed Melia’s entire body turning into a puddle of blood while her Sovereign Level blood puppets, whose numbers were now higher than enemy Sovereigns by a large margin, continued to attack.
Rune frowned, not knowing what happened.
Then suddenly,
"What is it?"
She heard a voice that made her jump in fright as she then turned around, only to see Melia staring at her.
"How- no, when did you come here—"
"I have placed blood marks all over the battlefield since I came here.
I can teleport anywhere I want to."
Melia revealed, and Rune just stared at this monster, not knowing what to say.
For the first time, the cat woman actually wondered if her Law was strong enough to be amongst this bunch of monsters.

chapters.title: Chapter 1841: Where are they?
paragraphs: While Rune’s mind was filled with doubts,
"Be quick, my blood puppets might be strong, but they still aren’t strong enough to take on Sovereigns with Laws without my presence."
Melia’s words rang in her head, pulling her out of her reverie.
"R-Right, I apologize.
I called you because I need your help."
"What is it?"
"Do you see those six of them?
They are Peak Divine Stage Cultivators who are after Ember."
"You should know they are not her match."
Melia frowned.

"I know that, they are not the ones I am worried about. It is those artifacts in their hands. They are rushing at her even in a situation where the number of their soldiers is declining at a rapid rate.
It feels like a desperate attempt…
Or even the last resort."
Rune explained what worried her, and Melia turned silent.

The Vampire knew that her sister was strong, but these artifacts came from the Factions behind these Worlds, and if it was really a desperate last attempt like Rune thought, then this might be a problem.
Melia also knew that Rune’s instincts were much sharper than anyone else’s because of her Law, so if she was worried, it was better to look into it.
"What do you want me to do?"
Melia questioned.
"I cannot find out what that Artifact is because I do not know their language, so I need your help. Charm an enemy Commander and find out what it is."
"So you want me to attack an enemy commander?"
Melia questioned, her eyes fell on the Unit Commander her army was fighting.
"No, you don’t have to fight anyone, just charm him."
Rune spoke as she pulled out an Infernik Commander, who was barely conscious and was bound with several Runic Chains, from the Core.
The Runic Chains were a magic artifact the mercenary used to neutralize and capture their targets, and seeing an enemy commander bound by these chains, Melia was taken aback.
Soon, however, she returned to her senses when she realized who she was standing in front of.
The cat could defeat him even without Ember’s boost. Now that she was strengthened by it, Melia highly doubted any normal Sovereign would be able to take her on.
"I kept him alive for you. Also tortured him a bit to weaken his mind."
Rune added casually.
Melia nodded as she grabbed the Infernik’s horn and her crimson eyes shined brightly,
[You will tell me what I wish to know.]
The order was passed, and the Infernik, having no way to resist, could only nod.

One had to know, all of this was happening in the middle of the battlefield. The allies and enemies alike were staring at the women, who were casually manhandling the enemy commander as if it was nothing.
Enjoy more content from Freewebnovel
These women, however, didn’t care about the eyes around them.
Rune simply severed anyone who tried to approach them. Soon, Ember’s orders were passed, and the Velcrian Soldiers moved, making sure none of the enemy soldiers got near the two women.

"The Chains of Soul is an Artifact that allows the user to materialize ethereal chains around the target. The chains move with uncanny precision, wrapping around the target’s body to bind their limbs and restrict their movements. The higher the number of chains used, the higher the success rate in capturing the enemy.

The Chains are inscribed with runes that sever the target’s connection to their abilities. Once wrapped around the target, unless the artifact user is killed or a Transcendent Level Being interferes, the chains cannot be destroyed. They are immune to physical force, energy-based attacks, or any other abilities.
These chains can al—"
The Infernik commander started talking in a monotonous tone, and soon, the women stopped listening.
"Chains that work even on Primordials, as I thought, they are going to use these chains on Ember."
Rune muttered. She, however, wasn’t too worried now, and Melia knew the reason.
"We can simply kill the commanders if something goes wrong and free her."
Melia spoke, and Rune nodded. The Cat woman even wondered why her instincts acted the way they did when it was nothing big, but then, the Infernik commander continued.
"The Chains of Soul are bound to our Leaders, killing the Commanders will not free your ally."
"What…?"
Rune’s expression changed.
[How are your commanders using them if those artifacts are bound to your leaders?]
Melia questioned.
"They cannot use it."
The Infernik replied monotonously.
"If they are, that means one of the Leaders is with them."
The instant they heard those words, the women’s expression changed.
’Ember!’
Rune called out.
’I heard it.’
Ember’s calm voice was heard.
Rune and Melia turned towards Ember, and suddenly, the Dragon disappeared.
’This will be fun.’
Suddenly, Astaria’s voice was heard.
’What do you mean…?’
Rune frowned in confusion.
’You were wondering how strong she is, correct?
Watch.’
Astaria’s voice rang out in Rune’s head.
’With 300,000 Sovereigns and 700,000 Protectors under the effect of her Law,
This is Ember Leander, at her full strength.’
As Astaria’s words ended, Ember returned to her position.

Rune and the rest of the women frowned in confusion, not knowing what just happened, but suddenly, Rune’s ears twitched as she suddenly tried to find the six enemy commanders that were rushing towards Ember.
’Where are they?’
She questioned.
The rest of the women woke up from their reverie as they looked around, trying to find them, and just as Allura found one of them,
Ember’s voice rang through their heads.
’Dead.’
Yes.
Six Peak Sovereigns, probably the Strongest Sovereigns of Tandris, died just like that, within a second.
’Thank you for hyping me up, Sister Star.’
The Dragon chuckled.
’I am enjoying this as much as you are.’
Astaria replied with a smile as she sliced another enemy. Honestly, she had given this battlefield to Ember and her sisters.
There was no one strong enough for her to go all out here.
’Wait…’
Suddenly, Thyra called.
’If he said that the enemy Leader was with them, where did he go?’
The Assassin questioned with a frown on her face.
The rest of the women, even Ember, frowned, unable to answer her question. What the women were unable to see was a lingering shadow that had entered Ember’s Shadow.

chapters.title: Chapter 1842: Why are you here?
paragraphs: "…What in the hell is happening?"
Kaelgran, who was watching the battle, questioned in a dumbfounded tone.

He had come here to the enemy world, expecting a difficult and hard-fought battle where he and his soldiers would give their all, defeating the enemy in their home. He was even prepared to bravely die on the battlefield.
Yes, the stakes of this war were that high.
Even a Primordial wasn’t sure if he could keep his life, let alone the rest of the soldiers. Yes, they did tell their soldiers that they would win this war overwhelmingly with no casualties, but…
That was obviously a lie said to strengthen their battle spirits, no? Even a child should know that.

How can one win a war without casualties? Especially a war between two worlds with somewhat equal strength. From the beginning, the Velcria leaders knew that this war would come together with heavy casualties.

They knew that after this war, Velcria, even if they won, would never be the same again. The losses would be overwhelming, but there was nothing they could do. Forced by the higher-level worlds, it was simply a choice between participating in this war and having a chance at survival, or offending a middle-level world and being destroyed by a force they sent.
For Velcrian leaders, this was supposed to be the lesser evil—a war where hundreds of thousands of their bravest soldiers were supposed to perish.
But…
What in the hell are these women!?
Yes, the leaders knew they were exceptional.
The one that fought their strongest Sovereign before, and the one who was the current acting General, they knew these two women were exceptionally strong.
They were also the ones that gave them enough confidence to attack Tandris despite being at such a heavy disadvantage. However, the leaders still thought that the battle would be extremely difficult.
"Are we sure they are just Sovereigns…?"
Kaelgran questioned out loud.
Liora and Elaris didn’t say anything.
They were speechless.
Their soldiers had already killed more than 100,000 enemy soldiers, and barely a few hundred of their own had died.
This was unprecedented!
Something they didn’t even know was possible!
Enjoy new chapters from Freewebnovel
’A True Goddess of War…’
Elaris muttered inwardly as she stared at Ember floating in the sky. She could see how the soldiers were moving and overpowering the enemies. That was definitely not normal.
And it wasn’t just the ability to command the soldiers; her own strength was absurd as well.
That woman killed six Peak Sovereigns within a second. Those Sovereigns and everyone around them couldn’t even react to her before they were decimated.
If the woman named Rune was strong, she was on an entirely different level. A never-before-seen monster.
A being who could change the course of a war just with her presence alone.
’If only she can become our permanent ally. We would never have to worry about wars in the future. Her presence alone would ensure our victory.’
Elaris and the other leaders couldn’t help but fantasize.
Then suddenly, Elaris noticed something and narrowed her eyes.
"Liora."
She called out.
"Did you see that?"
"I did."
The Seraphyte nodded.
"We need to go."
Kaelgran spoke with a grim look on his face.
"It is too late."
Liora, however, shook her head.

They were about 10 kilometers away from Ember. Even if they could get to her in an instant, it would all be meaningless since the enemy would have more than enough time to get rid of her before they could close the distance.
They lost her.
It was regrettable, but at the very least, the woman completed her job.
The enemy Dreadborn was able to hide himself even from their senses. It meant that he must have used a considerable amount of energy.
If they surround him now, killing him wouldn’t be a big problem, and once it became a 3 vs. 2 battle, the war would be as good as over.

Sure, with the woman lost, there might be more casualties than before, but the Velcrian leaders were already prepared to lose a major chunk of their forces in this war. Not to mention, their soldiers had already taken down quite a lot of enemy soldiers. If they continue to ride this momentum, the casualties might be limited.
"Let’s go."
Liora ordered, this time not because they wanted to save Ember or something like that, but to surround the enemy Dreadborn leader and get rid of him.
The war was finally entering the final phase, where the world leaders were going to take over.
Or at least that is what the Velcria leaders thought.
But…
On the other side, something entirely out of their expectation was happening.
’Wait…
If he said that the enemy leader was with them, where did he go?’
Thyra questioned with a frown on her face, and while the rest of the women frowned in confusion, they failed to notice a shadowy being entering Ember’s shadow.
At first, Ember wasn’t able to react. Soon, however, her expression changed.
’Oh? You sensed me?’
She heard an eerie voice in her head.
Ember frowned, but then she decided to answer.
’It wasn’t difficult.’
She shrugged.
’As I expected, you are exceptional.’
The eerie voice nodded.
’You girls are quite a strange lot. You have caused much more harm than we were expecting. Especially you.’
’Yes, this is the first time I am hearing that.’
Ember nodded casually.
’You sound a little too calm.
Do you know who I am?’
The eerie voice questioned in a curious tone.
’Kaelith Morvaine.’
’So you do know me.
How are you so calm then? I am curious.’
’You would have killed me by now if you wanted to.’
Ember replied, and Kaelith laughed out loud.
’You are indeed different from the rest. I like you.’
’I have a husband.’
’A pity.’
Kaelith sighed.
’Why are you here?’
Ember questioned directly, not wanting to continue this foolish game for long.
’Come to our side.’
’We took a miss—’
’It doesn’t matter. I promise you rewards far richer than what you would get from the mission.’
’This was never about war.
If we fail the mission, we will lose our 100% completion rate. I cannot allow that, especially since this is the first mission I am in charge of.’
Ember shook her head, and suddenly, Kaelith’s voice turned cold.
’It is a choice between your completion rate and your life. Choose wisely.’
He threatened.
Ember, however, simply laughed out loud as she shook her head.
’See? This is where you are wrong.
This was never about my life.’
The moment Ember said those words, Kaelith heard another voice.
’I do not like when other men get too close to my wives.
Leave.’

Leave.’

He shouted, looking around with a frown on his face.
He was in what was called the Shadow Realm. Not many beings in this universe could access such a realm, and the Dreadborn’s unique ability, Shadow Walk, allowed them to access this realm.
A realm that exists beneath every being’s shadow.
Within this woman’s shadow, no voice but his and hers should exist unless…
There is another being in here who is capable of accessing the Shadow Realm.

While it was surprising that this woman was able to maintain her calm despite knowing who he was, what should be even more surprising was the fact that this woman was able to talk back to him.
Even if it was her shadow they were in, to be able to talk back would mean that this wasn’t the first time someone had entered the shadow, and if that was indeed the case…
Then Kaelith’s theory was correct.
There was someone else in here.
’Who are you?’

The issue wasn’t that there was someone else able to access the Shadow Realm beside him. In this vast universe, he wasn’t foolish enough to think that only the Dreadborns could access this realm. If that was the case, the higher-level worlds would have their eyes on them.

Kaelith was one of the Leaders of Tandris, closely connected to Tandris’s Will. Every time any otherworldly force entered Tandris, Tandris’s Will always informed him and told him where the otherworldly being was.
And right now, in the place Ember was standing, according to Tandris’s Will, there should only be one woman.
Tandris’s Will couldn’t sense whoever this being was, and this is what alarmed Kaelith.
Being able to fool a world’s Will—he never thought it was possible. If this person could pull it off, then it meant that he wasn’t a simple being.
He needed to be careful; one mistake here from his side could lead to a catastrophe.
’Did you not hear? I am her husband.
You are in my wife’s shadow, and I do not like it.
However, since I am a magnanimous person, I will give you one last chance.
Leave.’
Nux warned again.
This was his wives’ show; he didn’t want to interrupt it.
Watching his wives shine on the battlefield as they crushed their enemies felt exhilarating. It was a proud moment for him, and he didn’t want to interrupt it by involving himself in the matter.
Right now, Nux actually wanted the man to leave, return to his allies like nothing happened, and continue the war.
The Primordials should face the Primordials while his Ember led Velcrian soldiers to absolute victory.
That was the ideal outcome of this mission from his perspective. Something that shouldn’t be very hard to achieve…
But…
Suddenly,
’Heh.’
Kaelith laughed.
’I was almost fooled by you.’
And the instant Nux heard his words, he had the urge to facepalm.
’Why does nothing ever go like you want it to?
Is someone purposefully making things difficult for me?’
He thought as he looked around, trying to find that sadistic bastard.

He, however, wasn’t given too much time to think about it. Kaelith continued,
’You are brave, child. I will give you that.
To act like this even when you know who I am, I admire your boldness.
However, you have shown me something I cannot ignore,
So I apologize for not leaving.
I will be staying in your wife’s shadow until you answer all my questions.’
Yes, Kaelith had it all wrong.
The man’s logic was simple: if the person he was talking to was as strong as he thought, why would he bother wasting his time giving pointless warnings to him?
Why would his wives, who should be living lives of luxury, act as mere mercenaries, risking their lives?

Kaelith was sure that he had overestimated this man’s strength. Heck, this man might even be weaker than these women. After all, he still hasn’t come out even though his wives are risking their lives out on the battlefield.

As for being able to hide from Tandris’s Will, Kaelith was sure this man must be using some artifact. An artifact that would love to be in his personal treasury than belong to this man who hides behind his women.
’You are a coward.’
Kaelith lashed out, and while he was at it, he went a step further,
’You should be ashamed of yourself.
You do not deserve to have these excellent women around you, especially her.’
Kaelith’s voice then turned menacing and,
’These women deserve a better partner, someone who knows how to take care of them, someone like m-’
’I changed my mind.’
Before Kaelith could complete, he heard the man’s voice again.
Then suddenly, in the Shadow Realm where nothing but darkness could be seen,
Kaelith saw two golden eyes staring at him.
’You aren’t leaving.’
That was it.
That was how far Nux’s patience could bring him.
After this, it was only wrath.
’Make this as entertaining as you can. I should at least get this much since I allowed this guy to enter my shadow, no?’
Ember spoke, and Nux nodded with a smile on his face.
’Yes, my General.
Your loyal subordinate will make sure you are thoroughly entertained.’
Nux answered, and suddenly, Kaelith felt his entire body being grabbed by an unknown force. His eyes widened in horror as he tried to leave. However,
’Did you not hear what I said? I said you cannot leave.’
’YOU BASTARD!’
Kaelith screamed in anger as he released all his Aura, trying to suppress the being in front of him. The being, however, simply waved his hand, dismissing his Aura as if it didn’t exist.
’This might be a bit painful. I do sincerely apologize in advance.’
Nux smiled,
And with this,
Kaelith’s nightmare began.

chapters.title: Chapter 1844: The True War
paragraphs: "Let’s go."
Under Liora’s order, the three Velcrian Leaders moved, all of them appearing next to Ember, waiting for Kaelith to come out.

By now, Ember had explained the situation to the rest of the women as well, and the moment they found out that one of the enemy leaders had entered Ember’s Shadow, the women couldn’t help but pity the poor bastard.

Of course, they didn’t think about the man for too long and continued what they were doing. However, the moment they saw the three Velcrian surrounding Ember, as if waiting for something, they turned their attention back to it.
The women could feel it. This was the final moment, and the actual War was about to start.
The three Velcrian Leaders frowned in confusion.
From what they knew, Kaelith was never the merciful type, nor did he like to waste his time playing with his opponent. If it was a target he wanted to kill, he would kill them as soon as possible.
Then why…
Why was this woman still alive?
The three leaders glanced at each other, confused.
Suddenly, Liora noticed Ember staring at her.
"Ember, the enem–"
The Seraphyte tried to talk. Ember, however, completely ignored her words and turned back toward the battlefield, giving orders to the soldiers.

With the Leader back, the efficiency of the Velcrian soldiers increased again. The Tandris soldiers continued to fall at a scary rate, and Liora, who observed all that, couldn’t help but frown in confusion.
What was happening?
Why was Ember still alive?
Why hadn’t Kaelith made a move yet?
Actually, where was that damn Dreadborn?
"Liora."
Suddenly, the Seraphyte heard a voice.
She glanced at Ember, who had called her, this time without a hint of respect in her voice.
"While we were not allies, and I wasn’t expecting anything from the beginning.
It is still disappointing to see how quickly you abandoned me to die."
"No, I did no–"
Liora was quick to try and defend herself. Ember, however, just laughed out loud.
"It is alright, do not fret. I won’t go back on my words. I will help you win this War. Actually, I already achieved my mission by taking out one of the three enemies you were worried about."
At those words, the three Velcrian Leaders widened their eyes in disbelief.
"Y-You killed Kaelith!?"
Elaris questioned, unable to believe what she just heard.
Ember, however, completely ignored her words and walked away.
"Rejoice, the War is yours.
Go and get the other two on your own.
I will deal with the rest, but after this is over, do not expect to keep any relationship with our party whatsoever."
"Hey you! Answer me!"
Elaris called out, only to be completely ignored by the General again. The Sylvanix decided to follow her, however, Kaelgran grabbed her arm and shook his head with a solemn look on his face.
Liora, on the other hand, recalled something.
’As for Shadow Walk, well, if they try to move in your shadow, let them.
I wanna see what happens.’

These were the words that pink-haired woman used while she was talking about the Dreadborns. The rest of these women laughed back then, and while Liora did find it strange, unable to understand what she meant by that, she didn’t think too much about it.
Now, however…
She couldn’t help but stare at these women’s shadows, countless questions entering her mind. Once again, her mind recalled another detail she decided not to think too much about before.
’Those women are much stronger than we think.
Do you remember when I used my Aura to suppress Granson, my son?
That girl was near Granson when I used my Aura. Even if I didn’t intentionally target her, she should have still felt the suppression from my Law of Self.
At the very least, she should have fallen on her knees if not directly collapsed on the ground like Granson did.
But…
My Aura didn’t even faze her.
That woman didn’t even react to it.’
Liora gulped, and in an instant, the words, ’After this is over, do not expect to keep any relationship with our party whatsoever,’ became much heavier.

The Seraphyte felt like she would soon regret her actions. To correct her wrongs, she thought of going to Ember and talking to her. But as she glanced at her, she saw two beings she recognized very quickly standing in front of her.
The two remaining leaders of the Tandris.
Inferath Ragnorok, the Leader of the Inferniks.
And Malcharon Nyxshade, the Leader of the Nightveils.
In an instant, Liora appeared behind Ember, not wanting to make the same mistake again. Elaris and Kaelgran followed her actions and appeared behind Ember as well.
The three Primordials were prepared to protect the General. After all, now it was a 3 vs 2; it was a battle they could never lose. The Velcrian Primordials were confident.
"Where is he?"
Inferath questioned directly as he stared at Ember.
However, before Ember could answer, Liora stepped in between them.
"She is not your opponent, I am."
"Go back when I am being nice, Seraphyte."
Inferath narrowed his eyes.
"Make me."
Liora didn’t back down either.
"Heh. It was getting boring, I agree."
Kaelgran grinned as he clenched his giant fists.
Then, with a grin on his face, he questioned,
"Why is there just the two of you?
Where’s the last one?
Hidden somewhere?"
He laughed out loud, and the enemy Primordials could feel their mouths twitching.
"Don’t force us to do something we do not wish t–"
Malcharon spoke, however, before he could complete his sentence,
BOOOM
Kaelgran’s Aura burst out. He stared at the two Primordials and,
"Do your worst."
He was ready for it.𝑓𝘳𝑒𝑒𝓌𝘦𝘣𝘯ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝑚
He was ready for War!
But then suddenly, Inferath sighed as he closed his eyes, his voice heavy with frustration.
"We did what you told us to do, but now we’re unable to connect with Kaelith. I can still sense him—trapped inside this woman’s shadow, unable to come out.
This wouldn’t have happened if you hadn’t insisted we bring her onto our side.
Since it’s your fault we’re in this mess, I hope you can help us out."
Everyone else frowned, confused by the Infernik’s words.
Who was he talking to?
Before anyone could ask,
BOOM
An overwhelming Aura burst out, alerting the Velcrian Leaders. Explore more adventures at freewebnovel
’A Primordial…’
The three of them narrowed their eyes.
They finally realized it.
Why the two Tandris Leaders were so confident despite being outnumbered.
The Velcrian Leaders, however, were still calm. It was still a 3 vs 3; they could still win.
Yep, they raised a flag.
BOOM
Another Aura burst out, as strong as before.
"A-Another one…?
Four Primordials…?"
Kaelgran’s body shook. However,
BOOM BOOM
Two more joined the fray.
The air grew heavier with each pulse of power. It was as if Tandris itself was crying despite it being its reinforcements.
"This isn’t possible…"
Liora muttered, her composure cracking. Even the soldiers, who were overpowering their enemies, froze.
Just as the Velcrians began to adjust to the oppressive energy, another wave hit.
BOOM BOOM BOOM
Three more Auras blazed into existence.
"They are all Primordials…"
Ember murmured, her expression grim.
As if her words were a trigger, more Auras erupted in rapid succession.
BOOM BOOM BOOM BOOM
The battlefield trembled. The soldiers from both Tandris and Velcria fell to their knees, unable to stand up.
The Velcrian Leaders had solemn looks on their faces, their bodies trembling as cold sweat poured down their faces.
One, two, three…
There were a total of seventeen new Primordials who had just appeared out of nowhere.
The ’True War,’
It ended before it even began.

chapters.title: Chapter 1845: This is not our war.
paragraphs: "T-This isn’t possible…"
Liora stuttered, her composure cracking at the sight in front of her.
17 new Primordials…
In a war where even one Primordial made a huge difference, in a war where, after somehow dealing with Kaelith, one of the three enemy Primordials, they thought that the victory was now theirs,
Just seeing the sight of 19 Primordials standing in front of them was horrifying.
The enemies’ Aura was suffocating. Let alone their soldiers, even the Leaders themselves were trembling.
"This isn’t possible!"
Liora raised her voice.
"You do not have the financial power to hire 17 Primordials!"
It was the truth.

To be honest, even an elite force of 15 Primordials was enough to level both Velcria and Tandris together. The ten Primordials could easily take on the six Leaders, and the five Primordials were more than enough to take care of the rest of the soldiers.
That was simply how big the difference between the Primordials and lower-level beings was.

If Tandris had the power to hire 17 Primordials, they would have done this a long time ago. The war would have never continued for so many decades, and even if they only just hired these Primordials, it made no sense to wait until they lost hundreds of thousands of soldiers.
Something didn’t add up here.
Soon, Liora recalled Malcharon’s words:
’Don’t make us do something we do not wish to…’
She overlooked it as a dying man’s blabbering back then, but now… Liora realized that the Nightveil actually didn’t want to summon these beings.
Why was that?
Was it because they wanted to continue the war, play with their enemies before finally taking their joy?
No, they would have lost too many soldiers if they did that, especially since Ember’s powers made it absolutely impossible for Tandris soldiers to turn the situation around.𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Then why…?

Would not using the Primordials help them save their resources? No, just the Primordials’ presence alone ensured that they would get what they came here for. After all, for the Primordials, it didn’t make a difference.
As revolting as it was, to them, crushing Velcria was as simple as crushing a bug. It wasn’t something they would consider ’work.’
Then…
Suddenly, Liora thought of something…
What if… they wanted to keep the Primordials hidden? What if these Primordials were just here for their reassurance, making sure they did not lose the war?
’We did what you told us to do, but now we’re unable to connect with Kaelith. I can still sense him—trapped inside this woman’s shadow, unable to come out.
This wouldn’t have happened if you hadn’t insisted we bring her onto our side.
Since it’s your fault we’re in this mess, I hope you can help us out.’
Recalling Inferath’s words and his respectful tone, Liora finally found all the answers she was looking for, and her eyes widened in horror.
"Y-You…
You all came from the Faction!"

Take here, for example. These Primordials are probably sent by the middle-level world connected to Tandris.

For that middle-level world, which has tens of thousands of Primordials, sending seventeen Primordials won’t even make a big difference. However, in this war, it would lead to Tandris’s overwhelming victory.

’And what now? These people broke the rules.’
’They will be destroyed.’

’These rules are made by Supreme Worlds.

Nux replied.

’Does this mean we need to silence everyone here?’
Melia narrowed her eyes dangerously.
’Alright, alright, girls. No need to get heated up.’
Nux laughed out loud.
’Do you have a way?’

The Seraphyte turned towards him, and the man’s cold smile widened even further.
"I never said I would only target Velcrians."

Very well, let me make this clear:
None of you are leaving this place alive."
The moment he said those words, his and the other 16 Primordials’ Auras burst out, this time at full strength, instantly crushing all the soldiers on the ground.
The five leaders stared at the seventeen Primordials and prepared themselves.

It was about survival.
And as the tension rose even further, a voice was heard.
"E-Excuse me…"

Twenty-two Primordials turned towards the source of the voice at the same time, and their eyes fell on a cute auburn-haired woman, who was staring at them with a somewhat embarrassed look on her face.
"S-So… now that it has come to all this…
Can we leave?"
Skyla questioned in an awkward tone.
’Where are your manners? Say please.’

"Please…?"
Silence.
Absolute silence fell over the place.
All the Primordials stared at the woman with speechless looks on their faces, and it was not just because of the audacity of her question.

Twenty-two Primordials had released their Auras with full strength. Even the world itself was trembling with fear. All the soldiers were on the ground; some had even died, and in this situation…
There stood nine women, with absolutely no signs of discomfort or trouble on their faces, as if the Primordials’ Aura didn’t matter to them.

"Do you all wish to live?"

"We do."

Nux’s method might work!
"Alright."

"Than-"

The Leader spoke, pointing at Ember.

You can leave with me. I have been observing you all ever since you appeared, and I can see all of you would grow into excellent soldiers in the future.
Right now, however, I have an urgent need for that woman’s Law.
So I want you to capture her so that I can extra-"
"See? I told you this wouldn’t work."

’It was worth a try, okay?’

’What are you talking about? We definitely got something from this.’

’Reason.
We got the reason to kill all of them.’

"Missed me?"
